entries.h: Antwerp imported 1,590,026 carats of rough in July for $241,050,713, the lowest monthly volume in its five-year published series
entries.t: AWDC's own machine-readable monthly series puts July 2026 rough imports at 1,590,026.12 carats for $241,050,713, an average of $151.60 a carat against June's $88.63, a rise of 71.05% on this desk's arithmetic. The published series runs from January 2022 and covers 55 complete months; July 2026 is the lowest of them, June 2026 (1,834,966.27 carats) the second lowest and May 2026 (1,989,371.16 carats) the third. Against July 2025 (3,118,013.12 carats for $414,238,026) carats are down 49.01% and value down 41.81%. The May to July three-month average is 5,414,363.55 carats for $634,237,819, or $117.14 a carat; the series high is $183.74 in April 2022. July exports were 2,751,303.49 carats for $255,048,440, $92.70 a carat, or 1.73 carats out for every carat in. The per-carat figure is a trade-flow average driven by mix, not a price index.
entries.s: AWDC, Antwerp diamond industry data, monthly rough series, read 28 August 2026

entries.h: India's gem and jewellery exports to New Zealand rose 50.56% to $25.46 million, with gold jewellery carrying about 93% of the increase
entries.t: GJEPC published FY2025-26 New Zealand figures on 27 August at the close of a delegation running 20 to 26 August: exports of $25.46 million against $16.91 million, up 50.56% (recomputed 50.5618%). Gold jewellery was $17.47 million, up 84%, back-solving to about $9.49 million a year earlier and a rise of about $7.98 million against a total rise of $8.55 million, or about 93%. Cut and polished diamonds $5.76 million, silver jewellery roughly doubled to $0.91 million, imitation jewellery up 13.16% to $0.43 million, lab-grown diamonds up 2% to $0.63 million. Named categories sum to $25.20 million of $25.46 million, 98.98%. The India-New Zealand FTA signed 27 April 2026 has not entered into force. Delegation led by Vijay Mangukiya; Consul General Madan Mohan Sethi attended. Council data on its own trade, labelled as such.

entries.h: India's gold import duty raised ₹10,463 crore in 81 days and imports rose in every published month after the increase
entries.t: The rate went from 6% to 15% on 13 May 2026, stated purpose the protection of dollar reserves. Customs duty of ₹10,463 crore was collected between 13 May and 2 August, 81 days, about ₹129 crore a day on this desk's arithmetic. April imports, ahead of the hike, rose nearly 82% year on year; May rose nearly 34% with the duty in force for part of the month; June and July together were $6.13 billion against $5.81 billion, up 5.51% on this desk's recomputation. India buys 700 to 800 tonnes a year and exports finished jewellery to the UAE, Thailand and Singapore. Reports on 26 August (Outlook Business; Free Press Journal crediting Moneycontrol) say officials are examining a cut, with industry asking for 6% and silver and platinum duties under the same review; sourced to unnamed officials, no notification issued, the Ministry of Finance did not respond to a request for comment, and several outlets trace to the same original reporting. Labelled speculative.
entries.s: Outlook Business and Free Press Journal citing Moneycontrol, 26 August 2026

entries.h: Gold at ₹1.7 lakh per 10 grams means the ₹5,000 Raksha Bandhan gift ceiling buys 0.294 grams
entries.t: Diamond City reported on 27 August that Ahmedabad and Surat counters held Raksha Bandhan demand at record prices, putting gold at ₹1.7 lakh per 10 grams against roughly ₹1.02 lakh a year earlier (up 66.67%) and silver at ₹2.45 lakh a kilo against ₹1.17 lakh (up 109.40%), both on this desk's arithmetic. The outlet's own claim that precious metals more than doubled holds for silver and not for gold. At ₹17,000 a gram the ₹5,000 gift band buys 0.294 grams, and the 1.5 to 2 gram pieces reported selling fastest are ₹25,500 to ₹34,000 in metal alone. Jigar Soni, president of the Jewellers Association of Ahmedabad, reports strongest demand in rakhis, coins, crockery and gifts to ₹5,000; Param Begani attributes lab-grown popularity among younger buyers to gold prices; Ashish Zaveri credits a partial price correction and reports 9-carat buying among the young. Nine-carat is 37.5% gold against 22-carat's 91.67%, or 40.9% of the content. The outlet carries a secondary-research disclaimer on its price comparisons. No volume figure in grams was published.

entries.h: Laopu Gold's first-half profit rose 88.18% to 4.267 billion yuan, and the interim dividend takes 74.6% of it
entries.t: Laopu Gold (06181.HK) published interim results for the six months to 30 June on 25 August. The company reports two top lines and they must not be confused: sales performance, covering total product sales, was 22.779 billion yuan, up 60.6%, while recognised revenue was 19.808 billion yuan, up 60.3%. The difference is 2.971 billion yuan, or 13.04% of the sales figure on this desk's arithmetic, and summaries quoting 22.78 billion as revenue overstate the business against its own accounts. Profit attributable to owners was 4.267 billion yuan, up 88.18%; adjusted net profit on the non-IFRS measure was 4.317 billion yuan, up 83.6%, so the adjustment makes growth slower rather than faster. Gross margin rose from 38.1% to 41.3%, net margin from 18.4% to 21.5%. Basic earnings were 24.16 yuan a share against an interim dividend of 18.02 yuan, a payout of 74.59%. Offline stores were 77.8% of revenue, online platforms 22.2% and up 171.9%, revenue outside the mainland up 107.8%. Separately dated and not attached to these results: shares fell 23.76% to close at HK$302.20 on 28 July, the day of the profit alert, a month before this release.
entries.s: Sina Finance and Caizhongshe, on Laopu Gold interim results, 25 August 2026

entries.h: Movado's net sales rose 4.9% to $169.8 million in the quarter to 31 July, and net income was 4.10 times the prior year
entries.t: Movado Group filed its Form 10-Q on 26 August for the three months to 31 July 2026. Net sales rose $7.9 million or 4.9% to $169.8 million. Watch and Accessory Brands made $142.9 million, up 5.3%, and Company Stores $26.9 million, up 2.8%, putting the watch segment at 84.2% of the company on this desk's arithmetic. Inside the watch segment, licensed brands grew $8.3 million or 9.0% while owned brands grew $0.3 million or 0.7%. United States locations made $47.5 million, up 5.9%; international $95.4 million, up 5.0%, including $0.7 million of favourable currency, without which sales would have risen 4.4%. Net income attributable to Movado Group was $12.3 million against $3.0 million, or 4.10 times, and $19.2 million against $4.4 million across six months, or 4.36 times. Gross profit rose $13.3 million and gross margin expanded approximately 530 basis points, roughly 380 of them attributed by the company to sales mix, and gross profit included $3.2 million of IEEPA duty refunds received, a little over a quarter of the quarter's net income. The company operated 57 retail outlet locations at both period ends. Carat Capital reported on 26 August that Fossil Group's net sales fell 4.9% in its own quarter to 4 July; the two quarter ends are twenty-seven days apart and are neighbouring periods, not the same one.
entries.s: Movado Group Form 10-Q, SEC EDGAR, filed 26 August 2026

entries.h: GJEPC put nine customs grievances to Delhi's Chief Commissioner in Mumbai, and was asked for a flow chart of the rough trade
entries.t: The Gem and Jewellery Export Promotion Council met Manish Kumar, Chief Commissioner of Customs, Delhi, at its head office in Mumbai on 24 August, following Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman's nomination of him to meet the trade. GJEPC fielded Kirit Bhansali, chairman; Shaunak Parikh, vice chairman; Anoop Mehta, convener of the diamond panel; Ashish Borda, convener of PMBD; Mital Doshi, convener of BITC; and Sabyasachi Ray, executive director. The Bharat Diamond Bourse sent vice president Mehul Shah and customs convener Anup Zaveri. This desk counts nine distinct grievances in the council's own account: rough valuation assessments; repeated examination including continued 100% checking at Mumbai Customs; underuse of the Risk Management System and of importer compliance history; inconsistency between Mumbai and Surat; absence of specialised trade expertise in valuation, on the argument that a general valuer cannot reach a transaction-level market value for rough; misdeclaration proceedings arising from minor weight or description differences; detention of consignment exports and re-imports over small variations; the need for better coordination between customs and other government agencies, with greater consistency of procedure and clearer guidance for officers handling the sector; and inconsistent interpretation caused by frequent personnel changes. Corrected 28 August 2026: this entry and the article first said eight, omitting the inter-agency coordination concern. Kumar agreed a risk-based approach could reduce unnecessary examination while keeping safeguards against revenue leakage, said the concerns would be examined with the Mumbai and Surat formations, and requested a consolidated flow chart of the rough diamond trade process plus a comprehensive list of issues. No consignment count, detention figure, clearance time, relief or timeline was published, and this desk estimates none.
entries.s: GJEPC, via Heera Zhaveraat and Solitaire International, 24 August 2026

entries.h: Doyle New York takes $457,700 for a 12.46-carat ring, and an 1890 sapphire pair beats its book by 180%
entries.t: Doyle's Important Jewelry sale in New York was led by a 12.46-carat cut-cornered step-cut emerald cut, D colour, VS2, between tapered baguettes, at $457,700 against a $350,000 high estimate, which is $107,700 or 30.8% above the ceiling on this desk's arithmetic, and $36,733.55 a carat. Rapaport's report of 24 August, drawing on Doyle's own website, puts the whole sale above $8 million. A JAR ring of about 1980 with a 5.78-carat G VS2 cushion modified brilliant made $165,600 against $80,000 to $120,000, or 1.38 times the high. A Cartier Mahango Panthere necklace of more than 500 diamonds weighing about 30 carats made $133,850 against $50,000 to $70,000, 1.91 times the high. A pair of 1890 earrings holding an oval 4-carat Ceylon sapphire and an oval 4.17-carat Kashmir sapphire, each ringed by ten old-mine diamonds, made $140,200 against $30,000 to $50,000, which is 2.80 times the high and 180.4% above it, the widest margin in the top five. A Tiffany and Co. Fleurage bracelet, eight rounds of 10.80 carats and 439 smaller rounds of 25 carats, made $127,500 inside a $100,000 to $150,000 estimate, 15% below the high, the one lot of the five that did not beat its book. The five together made $1,024,850, at most 12.8% of a sale of more than $8 million. Doyle publishes no origin or treatment detail in the results this desk read, so the sapphires' laboratory origin call and heat status are unknown and are not asserted here.

entries.h: A Verdura brooch with royal provenance makes 23,750 pounds at Elmwood's, and a 1927 Van Cleef feather makes 75,000
entries.t: Elmwood's Auctioneers sold a Verdura unicorn-head brooch, about 1.10 carats of diamonds under a circular cabochon turquoise crown, made by Fulco di Verdura, for 23,750 pounds or $32,400 at its London sale of 19 August 2026, reported by Rapaport on 24 August. It belonged to Virginia Fortune Ryan Ogilvy, dowager countess of Airlie, a lady-in-waiting to Queen Elizabeth II for close to fifty years. Three lots named in the same report sold for more: a 1927 Van Cleef and Arpels Art Deco diamond feather brooch at 75,000 pounds or $102,229, an Art Deco Egyptian Revival tiara at 65,000 pounds or $88,595, and a Cartier tutti frutti brooch of about 1940 at 60,000 pounds or $81,780. The Van Cleef made 3.16 times the royal brooch on this desk's division. Each dollar figure divided by its sterling figure returns 1.36305, 1.36300, 1.36300 and 1.36421, so one conversion rate near $1.363 to the pound was applied across the sale rather than four separately struck prices. The four named lots total 223,750 pounds or $305,004. Elmwood's published no sale total in the report this desk read, so the four lots' share of the sale is not stated. Priced as jewellery the Verdura returned $29,455 for each carat of diamond content, which is the signature and the provenance rather than the goods.

entries.h: Kagem shows rough emeralds at the 13th India Rough Gemstones Sourcing Show in Jaipur, nineteen days and no published price
entries.t: The Gem and Jewellery Export Promotion Council's release of 25 August 2026 records the 13th India Rough Gemstones Sourcing Show opening in Jaipur on 24 August and running to 11 September, a nineteen-day window. Kagem Mining Ltd of Zambia is named as showing rough emeralds, and is the only source-country miner named. The council puts attendance at more than 60 Indian coloured-gemstone manufacturers, its own count and not independently audited. R.K. Chandan, Commissioner of Customs at Jaipur, was chief guest, with Jeevan Ram Dhaka, Assistant Commissioner of Customs at ACC Jaipur, Yogendra Garg, the council's regional chairman for Rajasthan, and D.P. Khandelwal, convener of its coloured gemstones panel. The stated purpose is to let Indian manufacturers buy rough at source without travelling abroad. Kagem is Gemfields' Zambian emerald mine, 75% owned with the Industrial Development Corporation of Zambia holding the rest; its higher-quality rough auction held in London across May took $26.8 million, clearing 36 of 37 lots and 183,385 of 185,135 carats at an average $146.08 a carat, as this paper reported on 24 July, and Gemfields took $102.9 million from auctions across the first half of 2026, up 72%, as reported here on 31 July. No value, carat weight, lot count, sale mechanism or result has been published for the Jaipur show, which does not close until 11 September.
entries.s: GJEPC release, 25 August 2026; Carat Capital, 24 and 31 July 2026

entries.h: A rough stone passes visual screening as natural at the Israeli Diamond Institute and is classified Type IIa by infrared
entries.t: The Israeli Diamond Institute's technology department, in an article dated 25 August 2026 on its own site and bylined to staff gemologist Sergey Lazon, reports a rough stone submitted on Tuesday 18 August whose recorded data matched expected parameters and which externally appeared to be natural rough. Microscopy found small clouds and inclusions of the kind natural rough carries, together with minor defects the institute describes as atypical of natural diamond and consistent with CVD growth. A dedicated CVD screening device returned a preliminary indication of laboratory origin, which the institute itself qualifies by noting such devices can give ambiguous readings where inclusions are weak. Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy returned what the institute calls an unambiguous result and classified the stone as Type IIa, the nitrogen-poor category most laboratory-grown diamond falls into and one the institute says is difficult to attribute to natural origin given this rough's structure and shape. The account gives no carat weight, measurements, colour, price or country of submission. It states that the Gemological Institute of America identified a comparable stone days earlier and attributes that to a report by IDEX Online rather than to the GIA directly, a claim hedged twice in the original and carried hedged here. Single-source: the testing laboratory describing its own test, with no independent outlet reporting it and no submitting party named.

entries.h: India runs a prototype indigenous HPHT press at IIT Madras against a $594 million import bill
entries.t: Diamond City, the Gujarati fortnightly serving the Surat trade, reported on 24 August 2026 that the India Centre for Lab-Grown Diamond (InCent-LGD) has completed successful trials of a domestically designed high-pressure high-temperature diamond press at IIT Madras and grown HPHT rough on it. The press is a prototype built under the 242 crore rupee research programme announced for IIT Madras in the 2023 union budget, three years before the trial. Components for a full-scale commercial press have been manufactured across units in north India and shipped to IIT Madras for integration, assembly and final testing. Gem and Jewellery Export Promotion Council sources put an official announcement of the capability as likely in November 2026 and the first full-scale press as expected complete by December 2026; every date is an expectation reported through third parties. InCent has issued no statement of its own and this desk found no English-language trade coverage at press time, so the item is carried single-source and labelled so in the body, in Plate I's note and here. India bought roughly $594 million of rough lab-grown diamonds from China and Hong Kong in FY2025-26 on the same report's figures, which it converts to more than 4,900 crore rupees, an implied rate of about 82.5 rupees to the dollar. On that implied rate the 242 crore rupee programme is close to $29 million, or about 4.9% of a single year's import bill, on this desk's arithmetic and the outlet's own conversion rather than a market rate this desk has verified. India already holds a commanding share of world production by chemical vapour deposition and Surat cuts and polishes more than 90% of the world's diamonds; the gap is HPHT press capacity, where China's scale has made it the supplier of record.

entries.h: Indian imports of Russian rough fell from $1,195 million to $307 million, and Surat dismisses a Yakutia cluster
entries.t: Diamond City reported on 24 August 2026 that Indian imports of Russian rough ran at $1,195 million in FY2022-23 and $307 million in FY2025-26, a fall of $888 million or 74.3% on this desk's arithmetic. Russia once supplied roughly 30% of world rough. The report states that an executive order signed on 6 August 2026 establishes a diamond-cutting cluster between the Republic of Sakha (Yakutia) and the Smolensk region, where Alrosa's Kristall cutting works sits; that Russia is preparing an 8% export duty on rough; and that miners will be obliged to offer rough and semi-polished goods to the cluster's domestic manufacturers before the open market. The outlet carries its own secondary-research disclaimer on that policy material and this paper attributes the detail to it rather than presenting it as a verified reading of the order. Dinesh Navadiya, chairman of the Indian Diamond Institute, and Surat manufacturers argue that Botswana and Russia have both attempted domestic cutting before without matching Surat's scale or cost, where more than 800,000 skilled workers process nine of every ten rough stones in the world. Dubai-based traders and Surat importers add that with demand slow and margins thin nobody is funding new factories or relocating cutters, and that the United States takes about 30% of India's gem and jewellery exports while Russian goods remain under sanction. The report gives no capacity figure, timetable, employment target or redirected volume for the cluster, so there is no quantity against which Surat's confidence can be tested.

entries.h: Rolex's Dallas school took 27 of more than 560 applicants, and America's watchmaker count is down 85.2% since 1953
entries.t: Matthew Burdeen, chief executive of Burdeen's Jewelry of Chicago, told Watch Insider on 14 August 2026 that the shortage of qualified watchmakers is one of the biggest structural problems in the watch industry, with intake barely replacing retirement while the installed base needing service grows; the Centurion carried the account on 18 August 2026. Burdeen's is building a 7,000 square foot watchmaking, service and operations facility due in 2027. Rolex's Watchmaking Training Center in Dallas took 27 students from more than 560 applicants in 2024, a figure Fortune reported and the Centurion cites, which is one place for every 20.7 applicants on this desk's arithmetic. North Seattle College's Watch Technology Institute accepts an average of 10 to 12 students a year on an eight-quarter certificate. The institute's own employment page returned HTTP 403 to this desk on 25 August 2026, so its outcome figures are carried from the trade press rather than verified at source, and two different quantities circulate, an 87% employment rate over five years of cohorts and a 91% completion rate; this paper prints neither as settled. Watch Insider's study of 25 February 2026 put roughly 44,000 qualified United States watchmakers in 1953 on Department of Labor and American Watchmakers-Clockmakers Institute records against about 6,500 in 2021 on Bureau of Labor Statistics figures, a fall of 85.2% across 68 years on this desk's arithmetic. Jason Champion of the AWCI put the imbalance at at least ten employers seeking a watchmaker for every watchmaker seeking work, and Switzerland's employers' convention has worked to a need for roughly 4,000 additional watchmakers. No brand publishes a median service turnaround and no trade body publishes an aggregate repair backlog, so the shortage is argued from intake and job ratios rather than from measured queues.
entries.s: Watch Insider, 14 August 2026 / the Centurion, 18 August 2026 / Watch Insider, 25 February 2026 / North Seattle College Watch Technology Institute (HTTP 403 to this desk, 25 August 2026)

entries.h: Provenance Proof marks polished melee with synthetic-DNA nanoparticles, and rough still defeats the method
entries.t: IDEX Online reported on 20 August 2026 that Provenance Proof, the independent subsidiary of the Gubelin Gem Lab, has begun marking polished melee diamonds with synthetic-DNA nanoparticles using goods supplied by KGK Suisse, the Swiss sales and service arm of the KGK Group. Daniel Nyfeler, Gubelin's managing director, presented the work at the 41st World Diamond Congress in Singapore in July 2026, the congress at which the Qatar Diamond Exchange signed the three Asian bourse agreements this paper reported on 24 August 2026. Each particle carries a unique synthetic DNA sequence encoding mine of origin, mining period and country of manufacture; the tracer is invisible to the eye and to an optical microscope and readable only on laboratory equipment. Rough resists the technique for two stated reasons: rough is cleaned in hydrofluoric acid or deep-boiled before cutting, which damages the protective material around the DNA, and cutting and polishing removes particles applied too early, so the current model marks finished goods sorted and processed in large parcels. The technology is already in commercial use on selected Gemfields gemstones. Outside-source divergence, disclosed and unresolved: IDEX reports these as emeralds and Diamond City's report of 24 August 2026 describes them as sapphires; Gemfields mines emeralds in Zambia and rubies in Mozambique and does not mine sapphire, which points to emeralds, but this desk cannot settle it from the sources it holds. Nothing published states a cost per carat, a proportion of marked stones still readable after a full cutting and setting cycle, survival through a retail repolish, or a route for a laboratory other than Gubelin to read the marker.
entries.s: IDEX Online, 20 August 2026 / Diamond City, 24 August 2026 (Gujarati) / Carat Capital, 24 August 2026

entries.h: India's gem and jewellery exports to Australia rise 16% to $374 million in FY2025-26
entries.t: The Gem and Jewellery Export Promotion Council's own bulletin, published 22 August 2026, puts India's gem and jewellery exports to Australia at $374 million in FY2025-26, up 16% under the India-Australia Economic Cooperation and Trade Agreement. By category, gold jewellery exports rose by more than 28%, silver jewellery by nearly 30% and coloured gemstones by almost 36%, all three ahead of the 16% total, so the categories not named grew more slowly or fell. ECTA was signed 2 April 2022 and entered into force 29 December 2022; Australia gives zero-duty access across 100% of its tariff lines, with 98.3% duty-free immediately. The India-New Zealand free trade agreement was signed 27 April 2026 and has not yet entered into force. The council's delegation, led by Vijay Mangukiya, convener for international exhibitions, travelled Sydney, Melbourne, Wellington and Auckland from 20 to 26 August 2026 and met Showcase Jewellers Group, an independents' buying group founded in 1981 with 126 members operating 155 stores in Australia and further members in New Zealand and Vanuatu. The market read reported from those meetings is that 9-carat gold is mainstream Australian retail while 18-carat sits in the premium and fine tier. The release gives no prior-year base, so FY2024-25 is implied at about $322 million on this desk's arithmetic, and no monthly or quarterly path is published. Single source: the council's own release on its own export data. A Jewellery Industry Fair in Sydney on 10 and 11 October 2026 is the next fixed point, with an India pavilion scheduled.

entries.h: Qatar Diamond Exchange signs the Singapore, Shanghai and Tokyo bourses, thirty-three days before saying so
entries.t: The Qatar Diamond Exchange signed memoranda of understanding with the Diamond Exchange of Singapore, the Shanghai Diamond Exchange and the Tokyo Diamond Exchange. Each was signed by QDE director Ghanim Nasser Al Saadi with the counterparty's president: Fabio Cascapera, Lin Qiang and Michio Iwasaki respectively. The agreements frame member introductions, bilateral visits and reciprocal participation in tenders, auctions and viewings, and commit the parties to the World Diamond Council's System of Warranties and to Responsible Jewellery Council standards. None of the three has been published and none is reported to carry a volume commitment, fee schedule or term. The signings took place at the 41st World Diamond Congress in Singapore, held by the World Federation of Diamond Bourses and the International Diamond Manufacturers Association from 12 to 15 July 2026. QDE announced them in a statement dated Monday 17 August 2026, at least thirty-three days after the congress closed, and Rapaport carried the news on 23 August, day thirty-nine. This paper reported the exchange's own launch on 28 July 2026, day thirteen, three weeks before the agreements signed at that congress were made public. For scale, Dubai posted $41.7 billion of diamond trade in 2025. QDE operates at the Ras Bufontas free zone with sorting, vaulting, independent valuation and tender rights, and Qatar joined the Kimberley Process as a full member in 2021.
entries.s: Rapaport, 23 August 2026 / Gulf Times, 17 August 2026 / WFDB congress announcement / Carat Capital, 28 July 2026

entries.h: Israel's first-half diamond trade breaks into four categories and the rough legs fell twice as fast
entries.t: Figures published on 16 August 2026 by the Israeli financial broadcaster Emess, in a report by Gadi Fox, give the first categorical split of a half-year this paper had carried only in aggregate. Net polished exports were $625.7 million against $804.5 million a year earlier, down 22.3%. Net polished imports were $531.3 million against $609 million, down 12.7%. entries.h: India's July gold imports more than doubled to $4.16 billion while ETF inflows fell 55%

MCX futures averaged 14.9 tonnes of daily trading volume in July, up from 13.5 tonnes over the previous three months, with turnover reported separately at INR214 billion, about $2.2 billion, up 9% on the month. The first two weeks of August added INR11.79 billion, about $124 million. The council marks the international benchmark up 9% in the first two weeks of August to $4,391 an ounce and Indian domestic prices up nearly 7% to INR151,744 per 10 grams; this paper's own mark of record on 22 August is $4,602.40, a further $211.40 or 4.81% above the level the report describes, so the restock window it documents has already closed at a higher price. entries.h: Three LBMA Good Delivery notices in seventeen days, every one of them a Chinese refiner
entries.t: Three changes to the London Bullion Market Association's Good Delivery Lists between 5 and 21 August 2026 all concern Chinese refiners and run in both directions. Shandong Gold Smelting was suspended from both the gold and silver lists with effect from 5 August, as an interim measure after the association invoked its incident review process following the company's addition to the United States Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act entity list, with the investigation still to conclude. Hunan Shuikoushan Nonferrous Metals Group, known as SKS, was suspended from the silver list with effect from 21 August, announced 20 August, following a modified assurance opinion issued by SLR Consulting for its FY2025 Responsible Silver compliance reporting. entries.h: Okavango Diamond Company names Yoram Dvash board chairman
entries.t: Okavango Diamond Company, Botswana's state-owned rough trading arm, has appointed Yoram Dvash chairman of its board, reported 20 August 2026. He succeeds Gape Kaboyakgosi, who left in November after five years, so the seat had been vacant for most of a year. Dvash stepped down as president of the World Federation of Diamond Bourses two months earlier, having held that office since 2020 and completed the maximum two consecutive three-year terms, and he was previously chairman of both the Israel Diamond Institute and the Israel Diamond Exchange. He said he looks forward to working with the board, management and the government of Botswana. Under the ten-year sales agreement signed with De Beers in February 2025, Okavango receives 30% of Debswana's production for the first five years and 40% for the second five, with a conditional five-year extension that would move the split to 50-50; the agreement in principle announced in July 2023 had projected ODC reaching 50% within the base term and the signed document does not. No revenue figure, tender calendar or strategic target was published with the announcement. This paper reported Dvash's succession at the WFDB by Mehul Shah on 15 July 2026 and Okavango's tender arrangement with the Dubai Diamond Exchange on 1 August 2026. Correction, 23 August 2026: an earlier version said Dvash remains chairman of the Israel Diamond Institute and the Israel Diamond Exchange; he was previously chairman of both.

entries.h: Vasant Mehta, GJEPC chairman from 2008 to 2010, has died at 81
entries.t: Vasant Mehta, a former chairman of India's Gem and Jewellery Export Promotion Council, has died at 81, reported 18 August 2026. He ran M/s V. Rameshchandra & Co in Mumbai. He was the council's vice chairman in 1991-92, vice chairman again in 2006-08 and chairman from 2008 to 2010, a term that spans the global financial crisis and the credit contraction it produced across India's cutting and polishing sector. He convened the council's banking, insurance and taxation committee for years afterwards and advised the legal committee of the Bharat Diamond Bourse. Internationally he represented Indian interests at the World Diamond Council, the World Federation of Diamond Bourses, the International Diamond Manufacturers Association, the World Jewellery Confederation and the Kimberley Process, and he served the Mumbai Diamond Merchants Association. Gaetano Cavalieri, president of the World Jewellery Confederation, described him as first and foremost a servant of the industry. This paper carries no independent verification of the date or circumstances of the death beyond the trade report and stated so in print.

entries.h: Finsch closes permanently after 59 years, having carried 34% of Petra's revenue
entries.t: Business rescue practitioners put a plan to Finsch's creditors on 7 August 2026 and it passed with the required voting thresholds, concluding that no viable outcome exists to resume mining. The mine entered business rescue on 29 May 2026 and production was suspended in June, so the distance from rescue to closure was ten weeks. Finsch generated about 34% of Petra Diamonds' revenue in fiscal 2025 and began producing in 1967, making this the end of 59 years of commercial mining. More than 90% of its output was below two carats, the band in which lab-grown stones compete most directly and natural rough prices have fallen hardest; Petra's own account is that lower diamond prices and a stronger rand overwhelmed the mine's revenue despite strong operating performance. A secured creditor has provided post-commencement funding for limited on-site activity including asset reclamation, and proceeds will be distributed by ranking of claims with that creditor ranking highest. Petra is now a one-mine company and is moving Cullinan toward larger, higher-value stones. This paper reported the suspension on 29 July 2026 and had not previously carried the permanent closure; the report is eleven days old as printed and says so.
entries.s: IDEX Online, 10 August 2026 / Petra Diamonds business rescue announcement via Investegate / TimesLIVE, 15 August 2026 / Carat Capital archive, 29 July 2026

entries.h: Zales publishes a 67% self-purchase rate among its core shoppers
entries.t: Zales, a Signet banner, announced a campaign called You Are The Occasion on 19 August 2026 built on its own finding that 67% of purchases among its core shoppers were made for themselves. The campaign is merchandised as three style stories: Everyday Elevated, covering tennis bracelets, rivière necklaces, ear stacks and solitaire pendants; Stacking and Layering, covering mix-and-match gold chains, bracelets, bands and pendants; and Bridal and Engagement, split into four aesthetics named Iconic Classic, Ethereal Romance, Grand Glamour and Modern Muse. Two of the three require no occasion at all. Campaign imagery includes men wearing watches, gold chains and other accessories, and the work runs in store and across digital and social channels. Amanda Rather, Zales' vice president of style and trend brand marketing, framed the intent as helping women make their own rules and celebrate themselves. The campaign iterates on the retailer's Own It campaign of last year rather than opening new ground, which this paper stated in print.
entries.s: National Jeweler, 19 August 2026 / Signet Jewelers newsroom / Carat Capital archive, 12 August 2026

entries.h: China's lab-grown diamond exports rose 65.3% in the first half on semiconductor demand
entries.t: Shanghai Customs data reported through the Shanghai Diamond Exchange, China's sole general-trade diamond platform, puts first-half 2026 lab-grown diamond exports at 1.41 billion yuan, about $210 million, up 65.3%. This desk's arithmetic on the two published figures implies about 6.71 yuan to the dollar, offered as a check on the pair rather than as a currency quotation. The demand is industrial rather than ornamental: synthetic diamond is being bought as heat spreaders and substrates in advanced semiconductors, where its thermal conductivity is roughly five times that of copper, with Nvidia's February 2026 announcement that its next-generation graphics processors would use a diamond composite material with liquid cooling named as the catalyst. Approximately 80% of global lab-grown production still goes to jewellery. This paper's own tape carried the one-carat lab-grown reference at $703 on 21 August 2026, down a dollar on the day and down from $705 on 20 August, on CaratRadar. The two markets are supplied by the same reactors, which is the reason the paper ran the two facts together.
entries.s: IDEX Online, 12 August 2026 (Shanghai Customs data via the Shanghai Diamond Exchange) / CaratRadar, read 21 August 2026

entries.h: Lucara sells the 2,488-carat Motswedi and publishes no price
entries.t: Lucara Diamond has sold the Motswedi, recovered at Karowe in Botswana in 2024 and the second-largest diamond ever found, at an undisclosed price, reported 11 August 2026. The stone weighed 2,488 carats after cleaning against the 2,492 carats first reported. Proceeds sit inside the company's second-quarter results rather than being disclosed separately; Lucara reported $41.0 million of second-quarter revenue, down 6% on $43.7 million a year earlier, which bounds the stone without pricing it. Chief executive William Lamb has said the Motswedi was not as white as the 1,109-carat Lesedi La Rona and contained inclusions reflecting brown tones. The Lesedi La Rona, also from Karowe, was bought by Graff for $53 million in 2017 and is the comparison the market is left with, nine years old and describing a whiter stone in a different market. This paper reported on 12 August 2026 that Lucara's price per carat rose 24% in the same period while diamond prices generally fell.
entries.s: IDEX Online, 11 August 2026 / Carat Capital archive, 12 August and 15 July 2026

entries.h: Russia defers its 8% rough export duty to 1 March 2027, to start with the cluster decree
entries.t: A Russian government resolution published on 11 August 2026 moved the 8% export duty on rough and partially processed diamonds leaving the customs territory of the Eurasian Economic Union from 1 September 2026 to 1 March 2027, the date the country's cluster decree takes effect, so the two measures now begin together. Alrosa accounts for roughly 90% of Russia's domestic production. Rapaport reported on 11 August 2026 that the duty would have an impact of 3.12 billion roubles, about $37.9 million, on Alrosa's profit; that estimate was published while the duty was still due to start on 1 September, so it describes an annualised impact rather than a bill falling in this financial year. An outside-source divergence is printed in full rather than resolved: Rapaport and IDEX describe the duty as applying to rough above 0.45 carats including special-size goods over 10.8 carats, a floor with no ceiling, while TASS describes it as applying to rough between 0.45 and 10.8 carats plus special sizes, a band. The difference decides whether the largest Russian rough is taxed or exempt. The cluster decree replaces Russia's open rough sales model with a system in which miners must first offer goods to cutters inside the cluster before selling elsewhere.
entries.s: TASS, 11 August 2026 / IDEX Online, 18 August 2026 / Rapaport, 11 August 2026 / Carat Capital archive, 6 August 2026

entries.h: Jewelers Mutual names Mike Alexander chief executive from 1 January 2027
entries.t: Jewelers Mutual announced on 18 August 2026 that chief executive Scott Murphy will retire at the end of 2026 after twelve years, having joined in January 2015, and will remain a member of the board. Mike Alexander, president since 2025 and an employee since 2015, becomes president and chief executive on 1 January 2027, giving the trade four months of notice. Murphy's tenure took the company from a specialty insurer to a diversified platform of insurance and non-insurance businesses built on technology and data analytics, serving more than two million customers across the United States and Canada, and into Australia through the acquisition of Jewellers Loop. Alexander's responsibilities have spanned digital transformation, product innovation and market and portfolio expansion, and he sits on the boards of Diamonds Do Good and the YMCA of the Fox Cities. Murphy said leading the company has been the greatest honour of his career.
entries.s: PR Newswire, Jewelers Mutual release of 18 August 2026 / National Jeweler, 19 August 2026 / Insurance Journal, 20 August 2026

entries.h: Jean Dousset opens a third lab-grown-only store, at Westfield Valley Fair
entries.t: Jean Dousset opened its third store on 13 August 2026 at Westfield Valley Fair in Santa Clara, California, after a Los Angeles flagship and a New York showroom. This paper ran the opening against two other figures from the same day's edition: the one-carat lab-grown reference on its tape at $703, down a dollar, and Chinese lab-grown exports to industrial buyers up 65.3% in the first half.

entries.h: Swiss watch exports rise 9.6% in July and the seven-month year turns positive
entries.t: The Federation of the Swiss Watch Industry published July 2026 export figures on 20 August 2026. Total exports were CHF 2,628.3 million, up 9.6% on July 2025, and cumulative performance over seven months moved into positive territory at plus 0.9%, against minus 0.7% for the half on CHF 12.8 billion as this paper reported on 21 July 2026, a swing of 1.6 points. Wristwatches were CHF 2,522.7 million, up 9.8%, on 1,523,400 units, up 6.8%, or 97,000 additional watches. By material and by value: gold-steel plus 23.8%, other materials plus 11.1%, other metals plus 9.8%, steel plus 9.0%, precious metal plus 3.7%. Precious-metal units rose 0.9% to 37,100 pieces carrying CHF 912.8 million, which is 2.4% of wristwatch units and 36.2% of wristwatch value. This desk's arithmetic on the Federation's table puts the average export price of a precious-metal watch at about CHF 24,600 against about CHF 23,900 a year earlier, up 2.8%, and gold-steel at about CHF 4,970, up 29.5% on 4.4% fewer units. Markets: United States CHF 701.3 million, up 26.5%, a 26.7% share and a third consecutive month of double-digit growth; France plus 104.6%, which the release itself says does not reflect the actual trend in that market; Japan minus 3.7%, China minus 18.5%, United Arab Emirates minus 3.7%; the six largest markets CHF 1,563.8 million, up 21.7%, 59.5% of the whole. By price band on value, above CHF 3,000 plus 12.0% and CHF 500 to 3,000 minus 3.9%. The next release, covering August, is due 17 September 2026.

entries.h: India sets a $100 billion gems and jewellery export target for 2040 with no interim milestone
entries.t: India's Commerce Ministry convened a Chintan Shivir on 19 August 2026 and published a roadmap taking gems and jewellery exports from about $28 billion in 2025-26 to $100 billion by 2040. Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agrawal set out projections of 1.2% of India's GDP and 14% of merchandise exports by that year, manufacturing output roughly doubled to about 15 lakh crore rupees and overall economic value near 60 lakh crore, organised into five missions: global market access, MSME scale-up, an export-import fast track, Crafted by India, and next-generation talent and design. By this desk's arithmetic the target multiplies the sector by 3.57 times and requires 9.5% compound annual growth in US dollars read to the fiscal year ending March 2040, or 8.9% read to the year after, which is between 3.6 and 3.9 times the current rate. The Gem & Jewellery Export Promotion Council's own data, published 13 August 2026, puts gross exports for April to July 2026 at $9.17 billion, up 2.44% in US dollars and 13.58% in rupees; July alone was $2.35 billion against $2.34 billion, up 0.38% in dollars and 11.68% in rupees. By line for the four months: studded gold jewellery plus 21.09% to $2.24 billion, silver jewellery plus 72.19% to $508.18 million, platinum jewellery plus 17.20% to $77.82 million, polished lab-grown diamonds plus 7.47% to $408.50 million, plain gold jewellery minus 8.46% to $1.80 billion, and cut and polished diamonds minus 8.00% to $3.60 billion. This desk computes cut and polished diamonds at 39.3% of the four-month total, and the three fastest-growing lines at $994.50 million combined, under 11% of it. The roadmap publishes no interim milestone. Agrawal is quoted naming the mechanism as building a comprehensive ecosystem driven by innovation, global design leadership and trust.
entries.s: GJEPC (19 August 2026) / Times of Oman (20 August 2026) / GJEPC Solitaire, April-July 2026 export data (13 August 2026)

entries.h: A Rolex piece unique for Drake carries no published price; the priced Drake Rolex made $500,000
entries.t: Drake announced on Instagram on 16 August 2026 that he had received a one-of-one gem-set Rolex Daytona, described as an Ice Gradient piece unique, with baguette diamonds running into light and dark blue sapphires on the bracelet, sapphire-set bezel and lugs, paved dial and case sides, and the words Freeze the World engraved in blue enamel on the caseback. A dealer publication asserting the watch is entirely factory (15 August 2026) supplied no documentation and named a prior claimed one-off, a platinum Yacht-Master said to have been made for a Singaporean client in 2024, which if correct contradicts the first-ever framing; the same piece's $2 million to $5 million figure is explicitly its author's ballpark on a watch not for sale and is not carried by this paper as a valuation. The one transacted figure in the story is a Rolex GMT-Master II, reference 116758SANR, previously owned by Drake and seen in the video for a track from his 2011 album, which sold earlier in 2026 through the dealer Wind Vintage at $500,000, the full advertised ask, after four offers arrived shortly after listing, at approximately five times the average dealer value for the reference on EveryWatch data. Rolex operates no bespoke programme for clients; modification outside its own network voids the warranty and its service centres decline watches carrying non-original parts.

entries.h: Lab-grown wholesale prices are down 96% since 2018 while retail markups hold above 80%
entries.t: Edahn Golan's Q2 2026 lab-grown wholesale price list, published 7 July 2026 and reported by JCK on 10 August 2026, records the LGD Wholesale Price Index down 13% year on year in the second quarter of 2026, after a 26% decline across 2025, and down 96% since tracking began in July 2018. The decline is uneven by size: one-carat rounds rose 1% year on year, 1.50 to 1.99 carat stones fell 11%, two-carat stones fell 20%, and a three-carat VVS D colour round was quoted at $126 a carat, about 30% cheaper than in 2025. JCK reports US jewellery retailers' lab-grown inventory-to-sales ratio climbing from single digits in 2020 to nearly 50%, and retail markups exceeding 80% above wholesale in 2026, a difference of only one to two points from 2025. Paul Zimnisky is reported as holding that current retail margins are too high; Farshid Roshanravan of Rayan Gems is quoted saying there is no resale value for lab-grown diamonds; Edahn Golan is reported warning of a bullwhip effect and a possible offloading of memo goods. Against this paper's own tape, the lab-grown one-carat reference read $704 on 19 August 2026, unchanged, sourced from CaratRadar, and this paper's six-retailer sample of 25 July 2026 found $550 for the same stone, 21.9% below the tape figure. Corrected 20 August 2026: as first published this passage and the article said 28.0% below, which is the gap measured on the wrong base; $704 is 28.0% above $550. The source figures are nine days old at publication and that age is disclosed in the article.
entries.s: JCK Online (10 August 2026) / Edahn Golan (7 July 2026) / CaratRadar (19 August 2026) / Carat Capital archive

entries.h: Mountain Province sells 111% more carats at 44% less per carat
entries.t: In the three months to 30 June 2026 Mountain Province Diamonds sold 869,520 carats from the Gahcho Kue mine against 411,114 in the same quarter of 2025, an increase of 111%, at an average realised price of CAD 50 a carat against CAD 90, a fall of 44%. Carats recovered were 2,014,563 against 708,072, up 185% and the second consecutive quarter above two million carats. Cash cost of production fell to CAD 108 a tonne treated from CAD 167 and to CAD 48 a carat recovered from CAD 209. Adjusted EBITDA was CAD 8.4 million against negative CAD 2.2 million. The net loss was CAD 120.6 million, or 57 cents a share, against CAD 37.7 million and 18 cents, which is 2.8 times the quarter's revenue and about CAD 129 million below the positive adjusted EBITDA line; disclosed foreign-exchange losses account for CAD 11.3 million of that distance and this paper does not attribute the remainder. Chief executive Jonathan Comerford said the diamond market continues to face significant challenges. Two outside sources differ on the dollar conversion of revenue: the company's release gives $31.2 million and Rapaport $31.3 million against the same CAD 43.5 million. Release dated 13 August 2026, Rapaport report 16 August 2026.

entries.h: Sarine's first-half deficit widened 21-fold on a revenue decline of about $0.9 million
entries.t: Sarine Technologies reported results for the six months ended 30 June 2026 on 11 August 2026. Revenue was $14.4 million, down 6% on the first half of 2025, and the group recorded a net loss of $3.5 million against a net loss of $166,000 in the comparable half. No dividend was declared. Dividing one deficit by the other gives 21.1 times, this desk's arithmetic on the two published figures. Taking 6% off the published revenue implies revenue of roughly $15.3 million in the first half of 2025, which puts the revenue decline at about $0.9 million against a deficit that widened by $3.334 million, or approximately three and a half times the fall in the top line; those three figures are this desk's arithmetic on rounded published figures and are published by no source. The company attributes the wider loss to higher operating expenses, driven by a weaker US dollar against the Israeli shekel, and to reduced natural-diamond processing volumes in the face of lab-grown competition. Against that, revenue from GCAL grading rose more than 50% in the half, revenue from the MVP rough-planning service more than doubled, and Kitov.ai, the industrial-inspection associate in which Sarine holds 33%, booked $1.5 million of revenue and also more than doubled. The company's own framing is that a 6% revenue decline is modest relative to a significantly greater contraction in rough diamond supply. Sarine sells the scanning, planning and grading equipment and services that stones pass through on the way to a polished parcel, so its revenue tracks stones processed rather than stones sold at retail. This paper published global rough production down 8% to 98.8 million carats in 2025 on 27 July 2026, and Lucara Diamond selling 24% fewer carats in its second quarter on 12 August 2026. This is the first coverage of Sarine Technologies in this paper's archive.
entries.s: Rapaport (11 August 2026) / Minichart (11 August 2026) / Carat Capital arithmetic and archive

entries.h: Lucara's realised price a carat rose 23.7% while both its sales channels cut prices
entries.t: Lucara Diamond released its second-quarter 2026 results on 7 August 2026. The company sold 58,553 carats from its Karowe mine in Botswana during the quarter, against 77,167 carats in the second quarter of 2025, and recorded revenue of $41.0 million against $43.7 million, a fall of 6% on a 24% fall in carats sold. Dividing the published revenue by the published carats gives a realised price of $700.22 a carat for the quarter against $566.30 a year earlier, a rise of 23.7%; on the first half the same division gives $454.10 a carat against $493.21, a fall of 7.9%. All four of those per-carat figures are this desk's arithmetic and are published by no source. The company's own commentary states that average prices per carat declined across both channels, with tender prices falling 5% and Clara prices falling 17%, which it attributes to continued pricing pressure on mid-range and lower-grade stones. The whole of the realisation gain is therefore composition rather than price. It is not a function of more large stones reaching the surface either: specials, the stones above 10.8 carats, were recovered at 176 in the quarter against 242 a year earlier. Second-quarter net income was $15.6 million against $12.5 million; first-half net income was $1.0 million against $12.4 million, a fall of 92%, which implies a first-quarter loss of roughly $14.6 million by subtraction, this desk's arithmetic. The plant processed 761,848 tonnes of ore and recovered 90,082 carats at a grade of 10.9 carats per hundred tonnes, of which 6,973 carats came from tailings, at an operating cost of $23.76 a tonne, down 11% from $26.76. Full-year guidance was maintained at revenue of $100 million to $130 million, carats recovered and carats sold each at 340,000 to 360,000, ore processed at 2.6 to 2.9 million tonnes, operating costs of $27.50 to $31.00 a tonne, underground project capital of up to $110 million and sustaining capital of up to $11.5 million. Against $62.8 million of first-half revenue and 138,297 carats sold, that requires $37.2 million to $67.2 million and 201,703 to 221,703 carats in the second half, or 59% to 62% of the year's sales after the halfway point, all derived by this desk. Cash stood at $243.6 million at 30 June against bonds payable of $342.8 million with nothing drawn on the working capital or project facilities. The Karowe underground project has $275.9 million of completion cost remaining including contingency, with full production expected in the first half of 2028 and open-pit mining on track to conclude in the fourth quarter of 2026; in July 2026 the Botswana Department of Mines licensed the 15-person auxiliary winder and the 105-person man and material winder on the production shaft.
entries.s: Lucara Diamond Q2 2026 results via CNW (7 August 2026) / Rapaport / Carat Capital arithmetic

Palladium was handled identically, the tape carrying $1,351.00 against $1,368.00 on Kitco and $1,392.59 on JM Bullion at 00:13, a spread of about 3.1%.
entries.s: Kitco / TradingEconomics / JM Bullion / Carat Capital tape and arithmetic

entries.h: Signet gives Zales and Banter to Mattel's former global head of dolls
entries.t: Signet Jewelers announced on 11 August 2026, from Hamilton, Bermuda, that Jamie Cygielman has been named president of Zales and Banter, effective 24 August 2026. She will be based in Dallas and reports directly to J.K. Symancyk, Signet's chief executive officer. She joins from Mattel, where she was global head of dolls, a portfolio she reached after serving as general manager and president of American Girl and which she later widened to include Barbie. The same release named Pam Cloud president of Blue Nile with effect from 10 August 2026, based in New York City; Cloud spent more than 25 years at Tiffany and Co., latterly as senior vice president and chief merchandising officer, an appointment this paper reported on 6 August 2026. Two of Signet's four brand families therefore changed president within eight days, and the two appointments are different in kind: one seat was filled from inside the jewellery trade and the other from a toy company. Under Grow Brand Love, the strategy launched by Symancyk in March 2025, Signet is organised into four customer families: Kay and Peoples for core milestone and romantic gifting, Zales and Banter for style and trend, Jared for inspired luxury, and Blue Nile for luxury. The stated aim of the strategy is to have the company's chains operate as brands rather than as retail banners and to grow share in adjacent categories, notably everyday jewellery. Gold spot stood at $4,415.20 an ounce on this paper's tape the same morning, up 0.97% on the paper's previous mark of record and up 6.2% on the $4,158.30 the tape carried on 5 August 2026.
entries.s: Signet Jewelers (11 August 2026) / Forbes / Rapaport / Carat Capital archive and tape

entries.h: July's flat one-carat index hid a 1.7% gain in K to M colours
entries.t: Rapaport's Diamond Pulse for August 2026 published a colour-band breakdown of July's one-carat polished moves. One-carat goods in D to F and G to J colour, in IF to VVS and VS clarity, averaged a gain of 0.1% in July. K to M colours averaged a gain of 1.7%. K to M goods in VS clarity swung from a 0.1% loss to a 2.8% gain. This paper led its edition of 4 August 2026 on the finding that the RapNet Diamond Index for one-carat polished was unchanged across July, closing a slide that had run without a positive print since June 2025, alongside gains of 1.6% for 0.30-carat goods, 1.8% for 0.50-carat goods and 0.2% for 3-carat goods. The colour breakdown shows that the flat headline is an average of a near-flat top and a rising bottom, and that the recovery this paper has described as bottom-up since 14 July 2026 is running from the bottom of the colour scale as well as the bottom of the size chart. The ratio between the two bands is seventeen times, this desk's division of 1.7 by 0.1. The finding rests on a single source, and that source is the owner of the index reporting on its own index; there is no second publisher of RapNet colour-band moves against which to check it. The remaining figures in the same newsletter are already in this paper: global rough production down 8% to 98.8 million carats in 2025 was published here on 27 July 2026, De Beers' first-half revenue down 19% to $1.58 billion on 31 July 2026, and the Section 301 tariff bands of 10% and 12.5% on jewellery and gemstone imports on 25 July 2026.
entries.s: Rapaport Diamond Pulse, August 2026 / Carat Capital archive

entries.h: Two published references priced the same one-carat lab-grown diamond $61 apart
entries.t: On 11 August 2026 this desk read two public reference pages for a one-carat lab-grown diamond at the same hour. CaratRadar, republished that day, put the one-carat average at $711 and states on the page that its figures are asking-price averages by shape, carat, colour and clarity, calculated from active certified listings across major online retailers and refreshed daily. TheDiamondPrice, carrying an August 2026 date, put the fair market price of a one-carat round at $650, said most comparable stones sit between $590 and $760, and gave its benchmark as E to F colour and VVS clarity. The difference is $61, or 9.4% of the lower figure, derived by this desk. The two readings are not irreconcilable: the $711 asking average sits inside the $590 to $760 band the second page publishes, above its $675 midpoint, which is where an offer should sit relative to an estimate of transaction value. Neither page publishes the ask-to-sale distance as a number. This paper carried a third reference, StoneAlgo at $511 dated 7 August 2026, in its wire on 9 August; that page was not re-read on 11 August. Across the three, the published span for the same stone is about 39%. Lab-grown took 61% of United States engagement centre stones in 2025, a figure this paper published on 30 July 2026. This paper carries two lab-grown one-carat marks of its own and they differ: the newsroom tape carries $711, the CaratRadar asking-price average read on 11 August, while the site's tape chip carries $475, the midpoint of the published CVD wholesale band dated 30 July 2026 and locked by the build to the lab-grown price list it links to. Both are footnoted on the page with their quantity and date. A third figure of $727 was printed on the retail desk panel under the label "Lab-grown 1ct, wholesale" with no source or date attached, disagreeing with this paper's own wholesale midpoint under nearly the same label; it was removed on 11 August 2026 and replaced with the sourced $475. The RapNet Diamond Index and the Zimnisky rough index were both recorded as returning no numeric reading and both carried unreachable. Corrected 25 August 2026: RAPI publishes its index levels in plain text on its public page and this paper's tape carries the 1.00-carat series at 3,881.34, dated to the July 2026 point; only Zimnisky returns no numeric reading, and its status word is paywalled.
entries.s: CaratRadar / TheDiamondPrice / Carat Capital archive and tape

entries.h: The Dubai gap holds at AED 10.44 as all three readings move together
entries.t: On 11 August 2026 Kitco's live board at 06:00 New York time put gold at $4,372.80 an ounce, which is $140.59 a gram at 31.1035 grams to the troy ounce and AED 516.31 a gram at the dirham's fixed peg of 3.6725 to the dollar; both conversions are this desk's arithmetic and are published by no source. LivePriceOfGold's Dubai board, timestamped 11 August at 10:04 UTC, read AED 516.26 a gram for 24-carat gold, five fils from the peg figure and about one hundredth of one per cent away. Goodreturns' Dubai page, dated the same day, read AED 526.75 for 24-carat and AED 487.75 for 22-carat. The difference between the counter page and the peg arithmetic is AED 10.44 a gram, or 2.02% of the metal, against AED 10.66 on 10 August and AED 1.08 on 7 August, all three derived by this desk. Overnight the three readings moved almost in lockstep: the peg figure added AED 3.72, LivePriceOfGold AED 3.81 and Goodreturns AED 3.50, a spread of AED 0.31 across the three. That resolves the open question left by this paper's 10 August lead. The AED 13.25 step Goodreturns took between 7 and 8 August was a single repricing rather than a page that had stopped updating, and the margin it opened has since held through a rising metal. Under the one-price rule the tape carries the Editor's 06:00 press-time reading, written back over the 04:58 mark of $4,369.70, $64.60, $1,752.00 and $1,357.00: gold $4,372.80, silver $64.79, platinum $1,764.00 and palladium $1,362.00. Measured against this paper's own mark of record 24 hours earlier those are gains of 0.72%, 1.25%, 1.55% and 1.64%; Kitco's own session line at the same moment read gold and silver lower against its previous close, which is two conventions rather than two prices. The gold-to-silver ratio narrows to 67.49 from 67.84.
entries.s: Kitco / LivePriceOfGold / Goodreturns / Carat Capital arithmetic at the AED peg

entries.h: Kalyan Jewellers launches a Tamil Nadu-only banner, to be grown by franchise
entries.t: Kalyan Jewellers announced on 3 August 2026 the launch of Akshaya Thanga Maligai, a second retail brand intended to trade only in the Indian state of Tamil Nadu. The first showroom opens at Panagal Park in T. Nagar, Chennai, on 21 August 2026, selling hallmarked gold and certified diamond jewellery designed to regional preferences. The company has said it will expand the brand within Tamil Nadu through a franchise model before considering any other state, and has appointed the actor Sivakarthikeyan to support its visibility. Rajesh Kalyanaraman, executive director, framed the reasoning as regional markets offering significant long-term growth opportunities when approached with a truly local proposition. Kalyan Jewellers itself operates more than 400 showrooms across India, the United Arab Emirates, Kuwait, Qatar, Oman, the United States and the United Kingdom. No investment figure was disclosed. The choice of franchising rather than owned showrooms places the working capital for the gold inventory on franchisee balance sheets at a point when gold spot stood at $4,372.80 an ounce on this paper's tape the same morning. The demand backdrop previously filed by this paper is Indian gold jewellery demand down 15% by weight in the second quarter of 2026 to 75.1 tonnes, its lowest second quarter since the pandemic, with the value of that demand up about 50%, and Kalyan taking more than 46% of its June-quarter revenue in recycled metal and more than 55% in the month of June alone.
entries.s: The Retail Jeweller (3 August 2026) / Carat Capital archive

entries.h: Two Dubai gold pages read 2.11% apart on the same morning, and neither is wrong
entries.t: On 10 August 2026 two of the most widely quoted Dubai gold pages published materially different rates for the same metal on the same day. LivePriceOfGold's Dubai board, timestamped 10 August at 10:07 UTC, read AED 512.45 a gram for 24-carat gold, AED 470.43 for 22-carat, AED 448.40 for 21-carat and AED 384.34 for 18-carat, and states on the page that it prints a raw gold rate to which commission and labour charges are added. Goodreturns' Dubai page, dated the same day, read AED 523.25 for 24-carat and AED 484.50 for 22-carat, reporting no change against 9 August. The gaps are 2.11% on the 24-carat line and 2.99% on the 22-carat line, both derived by this desk from the two published figures. Kitco's live board at 5:57am New York time on 10 August put gold at $4,341.40 an ounce, which is $139.58 a gram at 31.1035 grams to the troy ounce and AED 512.59 a gram at the dirham's fixed peg of 3.6725 to the dollar; both conversions are this desk's arithmetic and are published by no source. That places LivePriceOfGold AED 0.14 from the raw-metal figure and Goodreturns AED 10.66 above it. Goodreturns' own ten-day table runs AED 485.25 on 1 August, 487.25 on the 2nd and 3rd, 485.50 on the 4th, 492.25 on the 5th, 510.25 on the 6th, 510.50 on the 7th, 523.75 on the 8th and 523.25 on the 9th and 10th: a step of AED 13.25 between 7 and 8 August against a metal move of AED 3.13 over the same span, then three flat days while spot continued to move. Read against this, the three UAE readings this paper printed for the 7 August session without choosing between them, Khaleej Times at AED 517.50, one bureau desk at AED 510.25 and another at AED 514.00, sit on two different lanes rather than representing three attempts at one figure; the peg arithmetic for 7 August gives AED 509.42.
entries.s: Kitco / LivePriceOfGold / Goodreturns / Carat Capital arithmetic at the AED peg

entries.h: India hallmarked 5.9 million silver articles in FY2025-26, nearly double the year before
entries.t: The Bureau of Indian Standards disclosed on 9 August 2026 that the volume of hallmarked silver articles in India rose to 5.9 million pieces in the 2025-26 financial year from 3.2 million in 2024-25, an increase of about 84% derived by this desk from the two published counts, and set out a plan to scale up testing and certification capacity to match. The bureau attributes the rise to consumers moving into silver as gold prices have risen beyond reach. About 230 bureau-recognised assaying and hallmarking centres currently handle silver testing across the country. The bureau's recognised laboratory network has grown from 147 in 2014 to 440, and government-empanelled laboratories from 24 to 350, against ten standalone bureau laboratories and roughly 270,000 product samples tested; the bureau holds about 700 mandatory standards out of 23,000 in total. Nishat S Haque, deputy director general for laboratories, said the referral and assay laboratory expansion would run across the next two years. Gold surveillance remains in-house while silver testing is outsourced to the recognised centres as capacity is built. Silver hallmarking has been voluntary in India since 2005 and no timeline has been announced for making it mandatory, so the 5.9 million figure counts articles voluntarily submitted rather than total production. A hallmark unique identification number for silver articles was introduced in September 2025. The demand backdrop previously filed by this paper is Indian gold jewellery demand down 15% by weight in the second quarter to 75.1 tonnes, its lowest second quarter since the pandemic, and Kalyan Jewellers taking more than 46% of June-quarter revenue in recycled metal.
entries.s: Bureau of Indian Standards via Business Today, Business Standard and The Daily Pioneer

entries.h: Etsy cuts 220 roles from product and engineering in a quarter it beat
entries.t: Etsy disclosed on 6 August 2026 a restructuring removing approximately 220 roles, about 12% of its marketplace workforce, falling mainly on the product and engineering organisation, at an estimated charge of about $35 million, primarily severance and benefits, to be booked in the third quarter of 2026 and completed within it. Approximately 1,600 employees remain. The company stated that the reduction is not a cost-cutting measure and is not related to artificial intelligence, describing the intent as flatter teams with wider remits, fewer handoffs and quicker decisions. The plan was announced alongside second-quarter results for the period ended 30 June 2026: revenue of $668.3 million, up 6.2% year on year against a FactSet consensus of $646.1 million; gross merchandise sales from continuing operations of $2.58 billion, with Etsy-only gross merchandise sales up 7.5%; a revenue take rate of 25.9%; active sellers up 5.9% to 5.7 million; and active buyers down 0.4% to 87.0 million. The reported net loss of $46.7 million is driven by $161 million of losses on discontinued Depop operations rather than by the core marketplace. Kruti Patel Goyal took the chief executive role earlier in 2026. Wedbush read the reduction as supportive of the gross merchandise sales trend. Jewellery and personal accessories is one of the six largest categories by gross merchandise sales in Etsy's own filings; third-party estimates place it near 30% of the platform total, a figure this desk carries as an outside estimate because Etsy does not publish a category split.
entries.s: Etsy Q2 2026 Form 10-Q / Reuters / Shopifreaks / MarketScreener

entries.h: QVC Group leaves Chapter 11 in 113 days having cut more than $5 billion of debt
entries.t: QVC Group formally emerged from Chapter 11 protection on 7 August 2026, having filed on 16 April 2026, a span of 113 days derived by this desk from the two dates. The restructuring removed more than $5 billion of debt. As part of the exit the company issued $1.2 billion of take-back notes due 2032 carrying a 10% coupon, disclosed in a regulatory filing, and secured a $600 million asset-based lending facility; the equity was approved for trading on Nasdaq under the ticker QVCG. David Rawlinson, chief executive since 2021, stepped down at the exit and was succeeded by Mike George, who previously ran QVC for more than a decade, as interim chief executive officer and board chair with immediate effect, alongside a newly appointed eight-member board. The company entered court with a pre-negotiated restructuring plan intended to compress the timetable, and the plan received judicial approval in July before the exit closed. Fine and fashion jewellery has been among the top-selling categories on the QVC platform, making the outcome directly relevant to suppliers who use long-form television demonstration as a volume channel. Alex Hennick, president and chief executive of A.D. Hennick & Associates, said the company still has brand recognition, loyal customers and strong vendor relationships. The 10% coupon on the new paper is the credit market's price for the business after the debt reduction and is carried here as the material figure alongside the headline cut.

entries.h: Pandora names Paulo Garcia chief financial officer, the third top seat to turn in a year
entries.t: Pandora announced on 6 August 2026 the appointment of Paulo Garcia as chief financial officer. Garcia joins the company on 1 October 2026 and assumes the role on 1 December 2026, succeeding Anders Boyer, who retires on 30 November 2026 after more than fourteen years with the company and remains until 31 March 2027 to support the handover. Garcia is a Portuguese national with twenty-five years of international executive experience across Europe and Latin America. He joins from the chief financial officer's role at Walmart de Mexico y Centroamerica, a separately listed subsidiary with about $50 billion of revenue and 240,000 employees, and was previously chief financial officer for Europe and Indonesia at Ahold Delhaize and before that at Unilever. The appointment completes a turnover of three senior seats inside twelve months at the largest jewellery company in the world by units: Berta de Pablos-Barbier takes office as chief executive on 1 January 2027, and Andre Branch was named president of the North America cluster in an announcement this paper filed on 5 August 2026 as pandora-fills-the-seat. None of the three arrives from the jewellery trade. Pandora's own published figures put the company at around 7,000 points of sale globally including more than 2,800 concept stores, and approximately 39,000 employees. The company sells lab-grown diamonds in eight markets, having added Spain and Italy in June 2026 with flagship stores in Barcelona and Milan.
entries.s: Pandora Group / WWD / FashionUnited / Carat Capital archive

entries.h: A 1983 Garrard 'Conundrum' egg makes £123,500, about five times its metal
entries.t: A 22-carat gold Cadbury's 'Conundrum' egg, named Cuckoo Cuckoo and made by Garrard & Co. of London in 1983, sold for £123,500, about $166,600, at Batemans Auctioneers & Valuers in Stamford, Lincolnshire on 1 August 2026. Forbes reported the result on 8 August and the auction house describes it as a world auction record for a bejewelled egg of its type. The price is close to six times the pre-sale estimate and about eighteen times the £6,500 the egg fetched at its previous appearance; Forbes dates that earlier sale to 2018 while the Batemans catalogue entry for the same lot is dated July 2017, and this paper carries both readings rather than resolving them. Forbes gives the egg at nine ounces of 22-carat gold, engraved and enamelled in translucent green, blue, orange and white with a cat, a weather vane, stars, mice, a castle and a treasure hunter finding a golden egg. At 91.7% fineness that is between about 7.52 and 8.25 troy ounces of pure gold, depending on whether Forbes means troy or avoirdupois ounces, worth roughly $32,600 to $35,800 at the $4,341.30 an ounce this paper's tape carries from Kitco's 5:00pm New York close on 7 August. That metal figure is derived by this desk from the reported weight and fineness and is not published by any source. Corrected 10 August 2026: this entry first carried 323.6 grams and about $41,400 of bullion, taken from a catalogue entry describing the secret thirteenth egg rather than the one that sold, and called the result four times melt; on Forbes's nine ounces it is about five times. The egg was one of twelve individually designed 22-carat eggs commissioned by Cadbury's in 1983 for a nationwide treasure hunt, with Perspex caskets buried across the United Kingdom each holding a clue to one egg; a thirteenth was made in secret. Greg Bateman, managing director at Batemans, called the eggs a fascinating piece of British cultural history.
entries.s: Forbes / Batemans catalogue via the-saleroom / Kitco

entries.h: The PBoC adds 640,000 ounces in July, its largest month since October 2023
entries.t: The People's Bank of China increased its official gold reserves by 640,000 troy ounces, about 19.9 metric tonnes, during July 2026, published with the monthly reserve data on 7 August. Holdings rose to 76.08 million troy ounces at the end of July from 75.44 million at the end of June, roughly 2,366 tonnes against 2,346. It was the twenty-first consecutive month in which the bank reported a purchase and the largest single-month addition since the 740,000 ounces recorded in October 2023. The gold reserve was valued at $306.35 billion against $303.72 billion a month earlier, within total official foreign-exchange assets of $3.419 trillion, up from $3.416 trillion, putting gold at about 8% of the reserve. Set against this paper's reporting of 2 August, which carried World Gold Council figures showing central banks buying 289 tonnes in the second quarter, up 62%, with China taking 33 tonnes across those three months, July alone runs at close to double China's second-quarter monthly pace. The same World Gold Council data put first-half central-bank demand at 345 tonnes, the smallest first half since 2022's 241 tonnes, after a first quarter revised down to 57 tonnes. July was also the month gold closed at $4,041.70, up about half a per cent and its first monthly gain since February, so the increase in pace came into a market that had barely moved. At the $4,341.30 an ounce carried on this paper's tape, 640,000 ounces is worth about $2.78 billion, a figure derived by this desk from the published ounce count rather than reported.
entries.s: PBoC monthly reserve data via The Private Banker and Bloomberg / World Gold Council / Kitco

entries.h: Shanghai brand counters run 348 yuan a gram above the exchange benchmark
entries.t: The Shanghai Gold Exchange's Au99.99 contract traded at 938 yuan a gram on the morning of 8 August 2026, up 7.53 yuan from the previous close. On the same day, Chinese brand counter prices for 24-carat jewellery stood at 1,286 yuan a gram at Chow Tai Fook, 1,285 at Chow Sang Sang, 1,284 at Lukfook, 1,283 at Lao Feng Xiang and Lao Miao, and 1,281 at Zhou Liu Fu — every major brand inside five yuan of the others and roughly 37% above the exchange benchmark, a spread of 348 yuan a gram. The same Mandarin financial-press tally puts the distance from the Shuibei wholesale price in Shenzhen, where most Chinese gold jewellery is made and traded, to the highest brand counter price at 170 yuan a gram. On 6 August the major brands raised counter prices by close to 60 yuan a gram in a single session, as reported by Sina Finance, against a far smaller move in the benchmark, reversing the pattern in which brand list prices lagged the metal. This paper declined to print a Chinese brand-counter figure on 7 August because two independent reads of that day's price stood at 1,240 and 1,297 yuan a gram, the main aggregator returned empty price cells and a second site failed on its certificate; the 8 August table, cross-checked against two independent brand-price trackers, resolves it. The demand backdrop, previously filed by this paper on 7 August, is China Gold Association half-year figures putting gold jewellery consumption at 132.13 tonnes, down 33.88%, against bar and coin demand of 339.34 tonnes, up 28.42%.
entries.s: Tencent News (Mandarin) / Sina Finance / China Gold Association via Carat Capital

entries.h: Swiss exports to Turkey rise 6.9% while the United States falls 14.8% across the half
entries.t: Federation of the Swiss Watch Industry figures for the first half of 2026 put exports to Turkey at 165.2 million Swiss francs, up 6.9% from 154.5 million in the first half of 2025 and 145.2 million in 2024, with Turkey the seventeenth largest market for Swiss watches. The figures were carried by the Turkish press on 6 August, sourced to the federation. Worldwide exports for the half came to 12.8 billion francs, down 0.7%, a total this paper filed on 21 July when the federation published it. The federation's country table shows the United States, the largest single market, down 14.8% for the half though still 2.6% ahead across two years; Germany down 10.5%, China down 5.0% and Japan down 1.6%. Against those, India rose 31.5%, Mexico 14.9%, South Korea 6.5%, the United Kingdom 5.8%, Hong Kong 3.3%, Singapore 2.2% and the United Arab Emirates 1.6%. France rose 63.4%, which the federation attributes to a logistics reclassification rather than to demand. By material, watches in precious metals fell 6.5% and steel watches fell 6.5%, while bimetallic models rose 20.0% and other metals rose 14.4%. Mechanical watches priced under 500 francs at export rose 23.8% while the 500 to 3,000 franc band fell 5.7%. Seven million wristwatches shipped across the half, up 2.3% in units, on a wristwatch value of 12.2 billion francs, down 0.6%. Turkey's 165.2 million francs represents about 1.3% of the half's total, a share derived by this desk from the published figures rather than published by the federation. This is the watches desk's first article since 4 August, after four consecutive dark editions.
entries.s: Federation of the Swiss Watch Industry / Turkish Minute / Hürriyet Daily News

entries.h: More than 46% of Kalyan's quarterly revenue came in as recycled gold
entries.t: Kalyan Jewellers reported consolidated revenue from operations of ₹10,589 crore for the quarter to 30 June 2026, up 46% from ₹7,268 crore a year earlier, and consolidated net profit of ₹349 crore, up 32%. The results were announced on 4 August 2026. Same-store sales in India grew about 28%, international revenue rose 35%, and Candere, the group's digital business, grew 112%. The company operates 524 showrooms worldwide, 354 of them Kalyan-branded in India.
