The company states that its gold-recirculation campaign, run under the name Shine with India, contributed more than 46% of revenue across the quarter and more than 55% in the month of June alone, reducing its reliance on imported gold. In the same week, MMTC-PAMP, India's only LBMA Good Delivery refiner of gold and silver, launched a limited-edition 10-gram commemorative coin on 4 August struck entirely from 999.9-plus recycled gold, capped at 8,000 pieces in assayer-certified packaging carrying unique identification numbers, unveiled in New Delhi by the Olympic silver medallist Mirabai Chanu. The volume backdrop, previously filed by this paper, is Indian gold jewellery demand down 15% by weight in the second quarter to 75.1 tonnes, its lowest second quarter since the pandemic, against a value up about 50%. A 46% revenue rise against a national tonnage down 15% therefore combines a price effect, an exchange effect and a store-count effect; the company's own same-store figure of about 28% is the comparable measure.
entries.s: Business Standard Capital Market / Indian Television / The Tribune

entries.h: P N Gadgil retires Litestyle for YOOU and sets a 100-store target for 2030
entries.t: P N Gadgil Jewellers announced on 8 August 2026 that it has replaced Litestyle by PNG, its lightweight diamond jewellery line, with a new brand called YOOU, offered in 9, 14, 18 and 22-carat gold and positioned for everyday rather than occasion wear. The line currently trades through 13 exclusive brand outlets across Maharashtra and Goa plus shop-in-shop counters across five states, against a stated target of 100 stores by 2030. Sara Tendulkar continues as brand ambassador, carried over from Litestyle. Saurabh Gadgil, chairman and managing director, described the brand as built for contemporary collections and everyday wear. The parent company reported first-quarter revenue of ₹2,413 crore, up 41% year on year, and has said it plans to open roughly 103 stores across its whole portfolio by the end of the current financial year. The segment context previously filed by this paper is that lightweight, low-carat diamond jewellery aimed at everyday wear is the most exposed category to lab-grown substitution: on 7 August this paper reported lab-grown diamond studs selling at $29.99 in the American mall channel. Two Indian jewellers filed news in the same week and both point the same way, Kalyan sourcing more than 46% of revenue from recycled gold and P N Gadgil building a chain around 9 to 18-carat pieces bought without an occasion, both responses to a gold price that has made the traditional heavy-gold Indian purchase unaffordable at the old frequency.

entries.h: July payrolls fall 23,000 against a consensus of 83,000; gold closes at $4,341.30
entries.t: US non-farm payroll employment fell by 23,000 in July 2026 against a market consensus of roughly 83,000 jobs added, a miss of 106,000, with June revised down to a loss of 20,000. The unemployment rate edged down to 4.1% while the labour force participation rate fell to 61.4%, its lowest in more than five years; average hourly earnings rose two cents on the month and annual wage growth slowed to 3.2%. The Bureau of Labor Statistics release page returned HTTP 403 to this desk, and the figures are carried as reported by Brisk Markets and CNBC on 7 August 2026 rather than from the primary release. Kitco's 5:00pm New York close on 7 August had gold bid at $4,341.30 an ounce, up $102.00 or 2.41% against Thursday's close; silver $63.46, up $2.06 or 3.36%; platinum $1,743.00, up $25.00 or 1.46%; palladium $1,357.00, up $4.00 or 0.30%. Fine gold at that level is $139.58 a gram against $138.72 at this paper's Friday morning mark; ten grams of 18-carat gold carries $1,046.85 of metal. Outside sources diverge on the day's gold mark and the divergence is recorded rather than resolved: Trading Economics carried $4,343.43 for 7 August, $2.13 above the Kitco close, and Reuters reporting during the session had spot near $4,356 at its intraday best. This paper carries the Kitco close because it is a stated closing print at a stated time. The CME FedWatch tool had September rate-hike probability at 46% immediately after the release, from 55% before it and against the 56.9% this paper carried on Friday morning. Consumer price data is released the following week. Saturday 8 August is a weekend and spot markets did not trade; the Editor re-read Kitco at press time and the reading matched the 05:00 tape exactly, so the tape stands unamended.
entries.s: Kitco / Brisk Markets / CNBC / Trading Economics

entries.h: Gold added $26.80 after the morning mark while platinum gave back $29.00
entries.t: Carat Capital marked four metals from Kitco spot at 5:58am New York on 7 August, an hour and a half before the payrolls release. Measured against Kitco's 5:00pm close the same day, gold rose a further $26.80 from $4,314.50 to $4,341.30, while silver fell $0.83 from $64.29 to $63.46, platinum fell $29.00 from $1,772.00 to $1,743.00 and palladium fell $25.00 from $1,382.00 to $1,357.00. In session-percentage terms platinum was up 3.14% at the morning mark and closed up 1.46%, surrendering more than half its gain; palladium was up 2.14% and closed up 0.30%; silver was up 4.71% and closed up 3.36%; gold alone improved, from 1.77% to 2.41%. The gold to silver ratio stood at 69.04 on Thursday's close, tightened to 67.11 at the Friday morning mark and widened back to 68.41 at the close. Platinum stood at 41.1% of the gold price in the morning and 40.15% at the close. Measured against this paper's marks of 5 August, the three-session move is gold +$183.00 or +4.40%, silver +$2.16 or +3.52%, palladium +$7.00 or +0.52% and platinum +$2.00 or +0.11%. Both readings are from the same source at two stated times and both were correct when taken.

entries.h: Bonhams sets three Chanel sales for September across New York, Paris and London
entries.t: Bonhams announced on 7 August 2026 a three-city Chanel auction series for September. New York holds Chanel: From the Vault II from 7 to 17 September, led by a gold-tone bird cage minaudière from Virginie Viard's Métiers d'Art Paris-31 rue Cambon collection, set with simulated turquoise and multicoloured crystals, estimated at $20,000 to $30,000; highlights go on view at the house's Manhattan flagship from 17 August. Paris holds Chanel: From the Vault II Paris Edition from 14 to 24 September with roughly 400 lots spanning Karl Lagerfeld's 1990s work to Viard's recent collections, led by a white tweed jacket from the autumn/winter 2025 ready-to-wear collection at €2,000 to €3,000, about $2,300 to $3,460, and including a Lagerfeld-era brooch with rhinestones and turquoise-coloured paste at €700 to €900, about $810 to $1,040. London holds Designer Handbags and Fashion from 21 September to 1 October and carries the heaviest jewellery weighting, with a private collection of Chanel costume pieces from the 1960s to the 1990s led by a filigree snake bangle made by Robert Goossens for Chanel Haute Couture circa 1960, estimated at $13,000 to $20,000, against a pair of Chanel Fine Jewelry Comète Géode earrings from 2024 in 18-carat white gold and diamonds estimated at £2,000 to £3,000, about $2,690 to $4,040. The signed costume bangle therefore carries roughly five times the estimate of the current-production gold and diamond earrings from the same maison, which prices attribution and documentation rather than materials. This is the first substantial auction-house announcement this desk has been able to file in three editions.

entries.h: HKTDC survey of 1,507 puts diamond first on demand and fashion jewellery first on growth
entries.t: The Hong Kong Trade Development Council surveyed 1,507 buyers and exhibitors at its twin fairs, the Hong Kong International Jewellery Show and the Hong Kong International Diamond, Gem and Pearl Show, which ran together from 29 July to 2 August 2026 at the Hong Kong Convention and Exhibition Centre. On the most-in-demand stone, 29% named diamond, 25% ruby and 20% pearl. On growth potential by segment, 57% named trendy fashion jewellery, 35% precious jewellery and 21% designer jewellery. Yellow gold was named the most popular precious metal by 40% of respondents. Respondents described themselves as cautious about 2026 and said they expect one to two years before confidence is fully restored. Hong Kong's own 2025 trade data provides the base: exports of fine jewellery rose 5%, driven by precious metal prices rather than units; exports of pearls, gemstones and rough diamonds fell 8%; exports of imitation jewellery fell 26%. The twenty-eight-point gap between the fashion jewellery and precious jewellery answers on growth is the widest signal in the survey and sits against a week in which gold closed at $4,341.30 an ounce, $139.58 a gram. Related context previously filed by this paper: China Gold Association half-year figures showing Chinese gold jewellery consumption down 33.88% by weight while bar and coin demand rose 28.42% (7 August).
entries.s: HKTDC via Rapaport / HKTDC Media Room

entries.h: US jewellery value rose 8.6% in the first half on a unit count that fell about 9%
entries.t: Figures from the analytics firm Tenoris, reported by JCK on 5 August 2026, put United States jewellery sales up 8.6% across the first half of 2026 while the average purchase price rose 19% and unit sales declined. June alone rose 13% year on year. Sales of items priced below $1,500 continued to decline. The implied unit change, derived by this desk from the published value and average-price figures rather than published as such, is a fall of roughly 9%. The composition reflects a spending distribution rather than a jewellery-specific trend: The New York Times has the top 10% of American households accounting for nearly half of all consumer spending, and a discretionary category inherits that shape. De Beers chief executive Al Cook, speaking at the JCK show, said larger and higher-quality diamonds are growing in value and desire. The same mechanism appears in three company results previously filed by this paper: Brilliant Earth's second quarter, revenue up 6% on total orders down 2.1% with average order value up 8% to $2,238 (7 August); Richemont's quarter to 30 June, jewellery up 24% within total sales up 20% and a seventh consecutive quarter of double-digit jewellery growth (15 July); and Luk Fook's record profit taken from fixed-price design rather than gram weight (5 August). The Knot separately reports six of ten brides in 2025 chose lab-grown centre stones.
entries.s: Tenoris via JCK / New York Times / company results

entries.h: NY Now closes its first show under Rockview with buyers up 5% and 96% rebooked
entries.t: NY Now's summer market ran from 2 to 4 August 2026 at the Jacob K. Javits Center in New York with 460 exhibitors, more than 70 of them new to the show or returning after an absence, across its Gift and Lifestyle, Jewelry and Accessories, and Home sections. Buyer attendance rose 5% on the previous summer edition. Organisers report a 96% renewal rate for the winter 2027 market and say 107 prospective exhibitors walked the summer floor to assess taking space. It was the first edition under Rockview Management Group, which acquired NY Now and JA New York from Emerald before that company's own acquisition by Apollo, and which has placed the industry veteran Dorothy Belshaw in charge. The winter 2027 market is scheduled for 31 January to 2 February 2027. Neither the attendance rise nor the renewal rate is broken out by section, so the jewellery-specific read is limited: NY Now is a gift and home market with a jewellery and accessories hall inside it rather than a jewellery fair. This paper filed the show's opening on 2 August. Separately and not filed as an article: Etsy is cutting 220 jobs, 12% of its workforce, in product and engineering, with second-quarter sales up 6% and first-half revenue up 5%; no jewellery-seller-specific impact has been reported and it is carried here as context only.
entries.s: Gifts & Decorative Accessories / National Jeweler / NY NOW

entries.h: India's lower house passes a fifteen-year tax exemption for foreign rough sellers
entries.t: The Taxation and Other Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026 passed the Lok Sabha on 6 August 2026, proposing an income-tax exemption for qualifying non-resident companies selling rough diamonds in India between 1 October 2026 and 31 March 2041, a fifteen-year window. The exemption is conditional on the sale taking place inside a Special Notified Zone; the two relevant zones sit inside the Bharat Diamond Bourse in Mumbai and the Surat Diamond Bourse. The class of qualifying seller covers miners, brokers, aggregators, auction operators and sightholders, and a qualifying company must furnish information when required. The existing regime offers a safe harbour presuming taxable profit at 1.25% of gross revenue, with Indian corporate tax at rates reaching about 33% of profit where the safe harbour is not elected. The stated policy aim is to reduce the movement of rough and encourage direct sales within India, positioning Mumbai and Surat against Dubai and Antwerp. The Gem and Jewellery Export Promotion Council welcomed the introduction. The Bill has cleared the lower house only and requires Rajya Sabha passage and presidential assent before any exemption takes effect; no date has been set for a hearing in the upper house, which makes the 1 October start date an intention rather than a commitment. For comparison, this paper reported on 2 August that a single tender cleared at 100% in Dubai against 75% in Johannesburg, and on 15 July that Dubai's diamond trade was worth $41.7 billion in a year.
entries.s: Rapaport / IDEX Online / GJEPC via Mines to Market

entries.h: All four metals rise on a fifth session, silver up 4.71% into the payrolls print
entries.t: At 5:58am New York time on 7 August, Kitco's spot page had gold bid at $4,314.50 an ounce, up $75.20 or 1.77% against Thursday's close, a fifth consecutive advance and above the seven-week high carried the previous day. Silver was bid at $64.29, up $2.89 or 4.71%, the largest single-session move of the four; platinum at $1,772.00, up $54.00 or 3.14%; palladium at $1,382.00, up $29.00 or 2.14%. The gold to silver ratio tightened to 67.1 from 69.3, more than reversing Thursday's widening. Against the 6:03am mark this paper carried on 6 August, gold added $43.60 an ounce or 1.02% and silver $2.62 or 4.25% in twenty-four hours. Fine gold at $4,314.50 an ounce is $138.72 a gram against $137.31 the previous session; platinum stood at 41.1% of the gold price against 41.0%. This desk wrote on 6 August that silver turning red beneath a gold high was the clearest internal warning the tape had printed all week; silver reversed that decline in full the following session, and the call is recorded here against the print that followed it. Context: Iran said it had reached an understanding with Oman on a proposed shipping route through the Strait of Hormuz, describing it as a temporary route and not a full reopening; ADP put July private hiring at 44,000 against about 50,000 expected, JOLTS was softer and initial claims rose to 199,000; the CME FedWatch tool showed September at 56.9% against 63.4% a week earlier. July non-farm payrolls were scheduled for 8:30am on 7 August, after this edition closed. Two divergences are recorded rather than resolved: this paper's own overnight tape read gold at $4,304.40 at 4:58am, $10.10 below the 5:58am bid, with silver at $64.16 and platinum at $1,763.00 and palladium identical at $1,382.00 on matching previous closes; and Dubai 24-carat retail was quoted at AED 517.50 a gram by Khaleej Times on 7 August, AED 510.25 by this paper's metals desk the same day and AED 514.00 by the overnight desk on 6 August. NAT1 and LGD1 were carried unchanged, the lab-grown reference holding at $709 on CaratRadar for a third straight day against $536 on StoneAlgo, a spread of roughly 24%.

entries.h: China Gold Association puts first-half jewellery down 33.88% and bars up 28.42%
entries.t: China Gold Association half-year figures, reported 6-7 August 2026, put national gold consumption at 511.41 tonnes for the first half of 2026, up 1.23% year on year. Gold jewellery consumption fell 33.88% to 132.13 tonnes while gold bar and coin consumption rose 28.42% to 339.34 tonnes, making investment metal roughly two and a half times the jewellery figure. The association attributes the divergence to elevated and volatile gold prices and to the rollout of new domestic gold tax policies, with temporary price corrections boosting bar sales through banks. These figures sit alongside, and do not match, the World Gold Council data this paper filed on 3 August, which put Chinese jewellery demand at roughly 136 tonnes across the half, a fall of about 30%, and the second quarter at 50.0 tonnes, the weakest since 2004. The gap between the two authorities is about four tonnes and nearly four percentage points, arising from differing definitions between a consumption series and a demand series; both are printed here and neither is preferred. Related context previously filed by this paper: Indian jewellery demand of 75.1 tonnes in the second quarter, down 15% by weight and up about 50% by value (31 July), and Luk Fook's record profit driven by fixed-price design rather than gram weight (5 August).
entries.s: China Gold Association via China.org.cn / China Daily / World Gold Council

entries.h: Brilliant Earth returns to profit on a bigger ticket and fewer orders
entries.t: Brilliant Earth reported second-quarter 2026 revenue of $115.1 million, up 6% year on year, on a 2.1% decline in total orders, with average order value up 8% to $2,238. Net income was $0.8 million against a net loss of $1.1 million in the same quarter a year earlier. Gross margin was 57.9%, a 360 basis point sequential improvement. Fine jewellery bookings grew 32% year on year. The company raised full-year revenue guidance to $459 million to $462 million and guided the third quarter to roughly flat sales with adjusted EBITDA between $3 million and $5 million. The composition is the result: revenue growth came from ticket rather than customer count, which concentrates the quarter in existing higher-income demand and leaves no volume growth underneath to absorb a trim in that cohort. The pattern matches other results filed by this paper in the same period, including US jewellery revenue rising while tonnage fell (3 August) and Luk Fook's fixed-price mix carrying a record profit (5 August).

entries.h: WPIC's 14% Chinese platinum jewellery decline is a base effect, not a demand fall
entries.t: The World Platinum Investment Council projects Chinese platinum jewellery demand down 14% year on year in 2026 and global platinum jewellery demand down about 6%. The council attributes the Chinese figure to an unrepeated and exceptionally high stock build in the second quarter of 2025, when Chinese fabricators bought platinum ahead of a gold price that had made their usual metal unaffordable; excluding that atypical inventory build, Chinese platinum jewellery fabrication would show a small year-on-year increase. The global 6% contraction reflects North American and European growth consolidating after strong years and Indian demand facing tariff-related headwinds, with the largest single contributor being the Chinese comparison. WPIC separately forecasts a fourth consecutive annual platinum market deficit for 2026, with supply falling short of demand by 297,000 ounces. Against this, platinum spot was bid at $1,772.00 an ounce at 5:58am New York on 7 August, up 3.14% on the session and standing at 41.1% of the gold price. The general caution applies beyond platinum: any 2026 comparison against 2025 in this trade is a comparison against a year in which buyers front-ran the gold price.
entries.s: World Platinum Investment Council via CME Group / WPIC press release / Kitco

entries.h: Claire's puts lab-grown diamond studs on a $29.99 piercing counter
entries.t: Claire's is relaunching its in-store piercing experience across the United States and Canada from August 2026, the second overhaul of that service in three years, and has expanded the starter stud assortment to include lab-grown diamonds and coloured gemstones alongside existing gold and steel options. Piercing kits start at $29.99 with the piercing itself free on kit purchase. The lab-grown range includes 14-carat white gold studs at 0.10 carats total weight, sold as complete kits with aftercare solution. The significance is the price tier rather than the material: at this level grown diamond functions as a finish and hypoallergenic setting specification rather than as a gemstone purchase, and the competitive displacement falls on cubic zirconia and surgical steel rather than on natural diamond. It is the clearest published evidence to date of grown material reaching mass-market starter pricing, and follows this paper's earlier coverage of grown wholesale price declines and of retailers tiering their floors between lab-grown for everyday and natural for rarity.
entries.s: National Jeweler / Forbes / Retail Dive / Claire's

entries.h: Gold makes a seven-week high on a fourth session up while silver turns lower
entries.t: At 6:03am New York time on 6 August, Kitco's spot page had gold bid at $4,270.90 an ounce, up $24.70 or 0.58% against Wednesday's close and its highest level in seven weeks, a fourth consecutive advance. Platinum was bid at $1,753.00, up $23.00 or 1.33%, and palladium at $1,367.00, up $20.00 or 1.48%. Silver was bid at $61.67, down $0.25 or 0.41%, the only one of the four lower on the session, after leading the complex all week with gains of 3.27% on 5 August and 3.2% the session before. The gold to silver ratio widened back to 69.3 from 67.8, undoing two sessions of tightening. Against the 5:58am mark this paper carried on 5 August, $4,157.80, gold added $113.10 an ounce or 2.72% in twenty-four hours. Fine gold at $4,270.90 an ounce is $137.31 a gram against $133.68 the previous session and $130.17 on 4 August; platinum stood at 41.0% of the gold price, down from 42.0%. This paper's own overnight tape recorded gold at $4,276.60 at 4:58am, $5.70 above the 6:03am bid carried here, and read silver as flat at $61.92 rather than down, a divergence recorded rather than resolved. NAT1 and LGD1 were both carried unchanged; the lab-grown reference was not printed as a market because two trackers stood 28% apart at $709 and $555. July non-farm payrolls are released at 8:30am on 7 August, the first full read on American hiring since the Federal Reserve held on 29 July with three dissents; June's print was 57,000.

entries.h: Alrosa swings to a half-year loss and prepares to idle open pits
entries.t: Alrosa's first-half 2026 accounts, as reported in English-language coverage of the filing, show revenue of 74.2 billion roubles, about $932.5 million, down 36% year on year, and a net loss of 10.67 billion roubles, about $134.1 million, against a net profit of 39 billion roubles, about $490.1 million, in the first half of 2025. Cost of sales fell 20% to 69.5 billion roubles, about $873.4 million, so revenue fell nearly twice as fast as the cost of production. The comparative half carried about 53.1 billion roubles, some $667.3 million, of non-operating income, including roughly 30 billion roubles, about $377 million, from the sale of Alrosa's stake in Angola's Catoca venture, which flatters the base. The company is preparing to place several open-pit mines into care and maintenance during 2026 and has suspended mining at Severalmaz, which accounts for roughly 10% of Russian diamond output. The 2026 production target of 25 to 26 million carats, down 14% from 29.7 million carats in 2025, is not new: it was set out by the company's head in December 2025, with the stated reason that it was not a question of capacity but of regulating demand and global inventories. For comparison, De Beers' consolidated average realised price fell 32% to $105 a carat across the same half, filed by this paper on 31 July. These figures rest on a single English-language report of the filing and no second outlet has yet carried them.
entries.s: Sada Elbalad / Interfax (Dec 2025) / De Beers Group

entries.h: Signet gives Blue Nile to a Tiffany merchandising veteran
entries.t: Signet announced on 5 August that Pam Cloud becomes president of Blue Nile effective 10 August, reporting to Joan Hilson, Signet's chief operating and financial officer. Cloud has more than thirty years in luxury retail, of which more than twenty-five were spent at Tiffany and Co., latterly as senior vice president and chief merchandising officer and a member of the executive committee. She subsequently founded Roseate Jewelry, a direct-to-consumer pearl brand. Signet acquired Blue Nile in 2022 for $360 million. The appointment places a merchant rather than a marketer in charge of a business originally built on price transparency for loose stones, which reads as a decision about assortment and presentation rather than traffic or conversion. It is the second senior jewellery appointment in a week and close to the inverse of the first: Pandora named Andre Branch, a consumer-brands executive with no jewellery background, president of its North America cluster from 15 August, filed by this paper on 5 August. Both new presidents start in mid-August, with the American fourth quarter already substantially bought.

entries.h: British buy-now-pay-later came under FCA supervision on 15 July
entries.t: Deferred payment credit, the interest-free instalment model underpinning buy-now-pay-later, entered the United Kingdom's regulatory perimeter under Financial Conduct Authority supervision on 15 July 2026. The market grew from about £60 million of transaction value in 2017 to more than £13 billion in 2024, with the FCA putting British usage at around 11 million consumers. Lenders entering deferred payment credit agreements must be authorised for the relevant consumer credit activities or hold temporary permission under the temporary permissions regime, and must carry out proportionate affordability checks before extending credit and give consumers clear upfront terms covering payment dates, amounts and the consequence of a missed payment. Consumers gain access to the Financial Ombudsman Service. Firms could register for temporary permission between 15 May and 1 July 2026 and have six months from commencement to apply for full authorisation. The relevance to jewellery is direct: most independents accept a provider's checkout plug-in rather than lending themselves, so the authorisation duty sits with the provider, but the January authorisation deadline is the point at which some smaller providers may withdraw. This is a three-week-old rule change filed now for its forward consequences, not news of the day.
entries.s: Financial Conduct Authority / GOV.UK / Reed Smith

entries.h: Onyx Partners bids $934 million for 117 J.C. Penney anchor stores
entries.t: Onyx Partners, a Boston-area private equity firm, has offered $934 million for a portfolio of 117 J.C. Penney stores covering 15.7 million square feet across 35 states, about $8 million a store or roughly $59 a square foot. It is the firm's second attempt; a higher offer of $947 million was rejected in December. Onyx states that financing is fully in place and that it is prepared to close on 25 September. The seller is Copper Property CTL Pass Through Trust, a Jersey City vehicle created after J.C. Penney's 2020 Chapter 11 filing with a mandate to liquidate real estate for the benefit of investors. The relevance to the jewellery trade is the anchor position: J.C. Penney has operated fine jewellery departments for decades, and anchor ownership determines footfall past every specialist jeweller in a mall concourse. An implied price near land-and-shell levels rather than going-concern retail levels indicates a market clearing anchor space on the assumption the current use may not be the final use. The transaction has not closed.

entries.h: Two thirds of American shoppers used an AI chatbot to shop in the past three months
entries.t: Attentive's holiday research, conducted online among 600 United States adults and published in the first week of August 2026, finds that 67% of respondents used an AI chatbot such as ChatGPT, Gemini or Perplexity to assist with shopping in the previous three months, rising to 80% among Gen Z respondents. Among AI users the most common activities were researching specific products, comparing brands and features, seeking recommendations and finding deals, with 51% using the tools to compare brands and almost three in five asking questions about specific products. On timing, 62% of consumers will plan holiday purchases before November, 71% expect to start shopping before Black Friday, and 46% plan to begin holiday shopping before November. Two limits belong on the figures: a sample of 600 adults surveyed online is small and skews toward respondents comfortable answering on a screen, the same population most likely to have tried a chatbot, and the survey measures consultation rather than conversion, with no figure establishing that a purchase was completed through a model. Related: the Natural Diamond Council has engaged the agency Artefact on how natural diamonds appear inside large language models, filed by this paper on 5 August.
entries.s: JCK / Global Toy News / Retail Dive

entries.h: Every precious metal rises for a third session as gold adds $109 an ounce in a day
entries.t: At 5:58am New York time on 5 August, Kitco's spot page had gold bid at $4,157.80 an ounce, up $81.20 or 1.99% against Tuesday's close; silver $61.35, up $1.94 or 3.27%; platinum $1,747.00, up $19.00 or 1.10%; and palladium $1,355.00, up $26.00 or 1.96%. It was the third consecutive session in which all four rose. Against the $4,048.80 print this paper carried on 4 August, gold added about $109 an ounce in twenty-four hours. The gold to silver ratio tightened to 67.8 from about 69.0 and platinum stood at 42.0% of the gold price; fine gold at $4,157.80 an ounce is $133.68 a gram against $130.17 the previous session. The move followed reports that the United States, Iran and Oman were closing on an interim agreement to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, with an announcement targeted for Wednesday; lower oil cut the inflation path and traders trimmed the odds of a September Federal Reserve increase to about 57% from about 67% a day earlier. Intraday prints were materially higher than the mark carried here, at $4,170.90 at 3:08am and $4,174.70 at 2:44am. Trading Economics printed platinum at $1,760.10 and palladium at $1,372.00, spreads of $13.10 and $17.00 against Kitco, which remains this paper's designated source. NAT1 and LGD1 both carried unchanged; the lab-grown reference was not printed because two trackers stood 28% apart, at $709 and $552, on the same week.

entries.h: Indian futures rise with the global bid rather than behind it
entries.t: October 2026 gold futures on India's Multi Commodity Exchange traded at ₹1,45,359 per 10 grams on 5 August, up ₹1,060 or 0.73%, and September 2026 silver at ₹2,24,109 a kilogram, up ₹2,494 or 1.13%. The same gold contract held above ₹1,43,500 in the previous session. ₹1,45,359 per 10 grams is ₹14,536 a gram of futures-grade metal, a duty-inclusive domestic price that cannot be compared directly with the $133.68 a gram international spot mark. Context: Indian jewellery demand fell 19% in the first quarter and to 75.1 tonnes in the second from 88.8 tonnes, a 15% fall, on World Gold Council figures filed by this paper on 31 July, with the council reporting demand beginning to recover in late June after a month-long lull. Chinese gold jewellery demand fell 28% in the same quarter to 50 tonnes, the weakest since 2004. Third-quarter Indian tonnage will not be published for months; the futures print is a price expectation, not an offtake figure.

entries.h: Hong Kong hard luxury grows four times faster than the city's retail market in June
entries.t: Hong Kong sales of jewellery, watches, clocks and valuable gifts reached HK$5.49 billion, about $699.9 million, in June 2026, up 20% year on year, on Census and Statistics Department figures published 4 August. Total retail sales across all categories were HK$31.49 billion, about $4.02 billion, up 5%, making hard luxury 17.4% of the city's retail spend and marking a fourteenth consecutive month of overall retail growth. Across the first half, jewellery, watches and clocks took HK$31.07 billion, about $3.96 billion, up 25%, against HK$203 billion, about $25.88 billion, up 10%, for all retail categories. The government attributed the run to continued economic expansion, rising local incomes and a steady increase in inbound visitors. The value line is flattered by a record gold price in a market that sells substantial volumes of gold by weight; Luk Fook's June quarter, filed by this paper on 21 July, showed retail value up 32% and gold same-store sales up 50% while diamond same-store sales fell 17% group-wide and 58% on the mainland.
entries.s: Census and Statistics Department via Rapaport / Xinhua / SCMP

entries.h: Pandora fills a six-month North American vacancy with a beauty executive
entries.t: Pandora appointed André Branch president of its North America cluster, effective 15 August 2026, succeeding Luciano Rodembusch, who left in February, leaving the seat vacant roughly six months. Branch joins from the chief executive's role at R.E.M. Beauty and previously held senior positions at Estée Lauder, L'Oréal, Diageo and Kraft Heinz across two decades in consumer brands; he has no jewellery background. Pandora describes North America as one of its largest and most important growth markets and states the brief as strengthening customer engagement, expanding reach and unlocking growth. The appointment follows a wider set of executive changes at Pandora North America reported earlier in the year. The American fourth quarter is already substantially bought by the time he starts.

entries.h: Luk Fook's record year was built on fixed-price jewellery, not on the gold price alone
entries.t: Luk Fook Holdings reported net profit up 88.7% to HK$2.015 billion for the year to 31 March 2026, its highest on record, on revenue up 29% to HK$17.21 billion, with gross profit up 42.9% to HK$6.31 billion and a gross margin of 36.7%. The results were disclosed in late June. The driver, stated in the Chinese-language financial press and largely absent from English pickups, is the pricing mix: sales of fixed-price jewellery, priced by the piece, rose 50.5%, while sales of gold and platinum products priced by weight rose 22%. Weight-priced goods pass the metal cost to the customer and earn the retailer a labour charge; fixed-price goods carry the margin inside the ticket, which protects gross margin when gold is at a record but caps revenue upside when volume returns and moves the price exposure onto the buying and hedging desk. This paper filed the same company's June quarter on 21 July, retail value up 32% and gold same-store sales up 50%, and its split on 22 July, diamond same-store sales down 58% on the mainland.

entries.h: The Natural Diamond Council puts 80% of its advertising behind consumers and inscribes a trust mark
entries.t: Natural Diamond Council chief executive Amber Pepper, speaking at a Gem and Jewellery Export Promotion Council meeting in Mumbai on Monday 3 August, said at least 80% of the council's advertising spend will be directed at consumers rather than the trade, and that the council's budget is significantly larger than the prior year, without giving a figure. She set out a Diamond Desire Index tracking consideration, purchase intent, sentiment and recommendation in India, China and the United States, with a baseline due September 2026, and a Natural Diamond Mark to be inscribed on natural diamonds and jewellery globally as a consumer trust device. Six transformational pillars were named: industry unity, category marketing, organisation evolution, consumer design, cultural relevance and category protection. The council is working with the agency Artefact on large language model optimisation. Pepper said the trade must stop talking about the crisis and start promoting the desirability of natural diamonds. Context: the RapNet Diamond Index for 1-carat polished was flat in July after thirteen months of decline, and De Beers' consolidated average realised price fell 32% to $105 a carat across the first half.

entries.h: Joopiter opens a standalone watch department with a rolling online sale closing 11 August
entries.t: Joopiter, the digital auction house founded by Pharrell Williams, opened Keeping Measure: Watches and Timepieces, the first sale from the standalone watch department it announced in July under Nate Borgelt, formerly of Bonhams. Lots close on a rolling basis through 11 August. The top lot is an Omega Speedmaster engraved for Alan Bean, the fourth man to walk on the moon, one of thirty examples of the reference produced after the first moon landing and distributed to President Nixon, Vice President Agnew and astronauts of the period; this is number 26, engraved for Bean's command of the 1973 Skylab mission, estimated at $250,000 to $350,000 with bidding at $230,000. Other lots include an HYT Moon Runner Red Magma from 2022 at $50,000 to $70,000 and a Ulysse Nardin with a Gay Frères bracelet from around 1960 at $15,000 to $25,000, alongside Patek Philippe, Audemars Piguet, Piaget, Cartier, Ressence, Speake-Marin and Ōtsuka Lotēc. The sale runs against an empty summer calendar; the next priced offering of note is Sotheby's Gem Drop in New York, 10 to 13 August. Watch auction sales reached $680 million in the first half, up 45%, with 73 lots clearing $1 million.

entries.h: The 1-carat polished index stops falling after thirteen months, and July prints the best month since the tariffs
entries.t: Rapaport published July 2026 RapNet Diamond Index figures on 4 August. The 1-carat index was unchanged across the month, ending a decline that had run without a positive print since June 2025. The 0.30-carat index rose 1.6%, the 0.50-carat index rose 1.8%, its largest monthly gain since March 2025, and the 3-carat index rose 0.2%. It is the first month since March 2025 in which none of the four headline categories fell, making July the best month for polished prices since the April 2025 tariff schedule. Rapaport reports American demand concentrated in 2-carat rounds in G to J colour and VS1 to SI2 clarity, plus fancy shapes. The tariff schedule in force from late July keeps 10% on polished finished in India while loose natural diamonds cut in Belgium, Botswana and Namibia clear at zero. Lab-grown competition at the entry price point, weak Chinese demand and Angolan rough surplus are unresolved. Carat Capital's NAT1 line carries 5,232.00 unchanged, now for the sourced reason that the 1-carat index was flat rather than for the absence of a print.

entries.h: Fancy colour diamond prices move one tenth of one percent in the second quarter
entries.t: The Fancy Color Research Foundation's index of pink, blue and yellow diamonds fell 0.1% across the second quarter of 2026, reported by Rapaport on 3 August. Pink rose 0.1% after falling 0.3% in the prior quarter, with 1 and 1.5-carat pinks each up 0.4%, 2 and 3-carat pinks each up 0.6%, fancy-vivid pinks up 0.5% and fancy-intense pinks down 0.1%. Blue fell 0.4% after falling 0.3%, with 1-carat blues up 0.7%, 1.5-carat down 0.2%, 2-carat down 1.3%, 3-carat down 0.7% and 5-carat flat; 1-carat fancy-vivid blues rose 1.5% while fancy and fancy-intense blues each fell 0.6%. Yellow fell 0.3% for a second consecutive quarter, with 3-carat yellows up 0.7% against fancy-intense yellows down 1.3%. The foundation described a market that remained broadly stable.
entries.s: Fancy Color Research Foundation via Rapaport

entries.h: Independent watchmakers clear more secondary value than LVMH's watch brands in the first half
entries.t: EveryWatch's first-half 2026 report, published 30 July and taken up by the trade press on 3 August, put global secondary watch transactions at $10.5 billion, up 37.2% year on year, compiled from sold prices at about 650 dealers and roughly 470 auction houses. Independent makers transacted $633.8 million collectively, up 89%, ahead of the LVMH watch portfolio at about $617 million. F.P. Journe accounted for $201.6 million of that, an increase of 196.9%, ranking seventh among all watch brands, on a median sale price of $215,000, up 82%, and a turnover rate above 57%. H. Moser and Cie. did $26 million, up 64%, Parmigiani Fleurier $21 million, up 60%, and De Bethune $19 million, up 2%. Rolex remained the largest single brand at $4.29 billion, about 41% of all value, with Patek Philippe at $1.51 billion and Audemars Piguet at $983 million. Rolex certified pre-owned reached $385 million, more than double the prior year. The United States and Canada transacted $4.5 billion, up 70%, while Asia fell 2.6%. The median watch sold for $5,900, up 19%, in an average of 43 days against 39.

entries.h: Swatch replaces the release-day queue with a 32-question form and takes 1.2 million applications
entries.t: Swatch allocated 1,969 MoonSwatch Mission to the Moon 1969 pieces through the Electronic Swatch Timepiece Application, a 32-question online form, and more than 1.2 million people completed it, about 600 applicants per available watch. The retail price is $570, derived from the gold price on 21 July 1969. JCK reports the watch carries 11 grams of 18-karat gold across dial, hands, crown and pushers, which is 8.25 grams of fine gold, worth about $1,074 at Kitco spot of $4,048.80 an ounce on 4 August. The mechanic followed the May Royal Pop collaboration with Audemars Piguet, which required police outside stores in New York, Paris and London, closed 15 American stores on a Saturday and traded at four to five times retail before falling below $400 by August. Swatch Group stock rose about 15% in the two weeks after the Royal Pop launch.

entries.h: Watch auction sales rise 45% to $680 million with 73 lots above a million dollars
entries.t: EveryWatch's first-half 2026 report put watch auction sales at $680 million, up 45% year on year, inside a total secondary market of $10.5 billion. Seventy-three lots cleared $1 million, close to three times the same period a year earlier, and three lots passed $10 million. The highest was an F.P. Journe Chronometre a Resonance Souscription number 007, which made $13,922,000 at Phillips New York on 14 June 2026, the highest auction price for a watch by an independent maker. Phillips also placed a Resonance Souscription number 18 at $6.3 million and a Resonance Pisa at $3 million across the spring season. The median watch across all channels sold for $5,900, up 19%, and took an average of 43 days to sell against 39 a year earlier.

entries.h: The white metals lead again as gold slips 0.14% ahead of Friday's payrolls
entries.t: At 5:59am New York time on 4 August, Kitco's spot page had gold bid at $4,048.80 an ounce, down $5.70 or 0.14% against Monday's close; platinum $1,655.00, up $28.00 or 1.72%; palladium $1,266.00, up $22.00 or 1.77%; and silver $58.63, up 56.3 cents or 0.97%. The gold to silver ratio tightened to about 69.0 from 69.8 the previous session and platinum stood at 40.9% of the gold price. Trading Economics, quoting a different print time on the same session, showed platinum up 2.56% and silver up 1.83% while agreeing with Kitco on gold at minus 0.14%; it put gold down about 2.8% over the past month and up 19.8% on the year, silver down 5.3% on the month and up 55.3% on the year, and platinum up 26.8% on the year. The ADP national employment report is due Wednesday and non-farm payrolls Friday, the first full read on American hiring since the Federal Reserve held rates on 29 July with three dissents. Gold at $4,048.80 an ounce is $130.17 a gram of fine metal.

entries.h: Vicenzaoro September opens Hall 2 and hosts CIBJO's centenary congress
entries.t: Vicenzaoro September runs from 4 to 8 September 2026 at Fiera di Vicenza, organised by Italian Exhibition Group, with roughly 1,300 exhibiting brands from 38 countries and buyers expected from more than 130 countries, on figures IEG gave JCK on 13 July. The show was reported close to sold out in late May. The new Hall 2, a two-storey central hub connected by covered walkways, is fully operational for the first time, and T.Gold, the machinery and technology section for precious-metal production, has moved inside the expo centre grounds into Hall 4; Jewellery Outlook confirmed both through interviews published 31 July. CIBJO, the World Jewellery Confederation, holds its centenary congress in Vicenza from 4 to 7 September, one hundred years after its founding in 1926, with its Assembly of Delegates and sectoral commissions meeting and amendments to the Blue Books introduced. The scheduled agenda covers the state of the diamond industry, lab-grown diamonds, the supply chain, pearls and coloured gemstones. Russia's Resolution 657, which bans the word diamond for synthetics sold there, comes into force on 1 September, three days before the congress opens.

entries.h: Vietnam's smuggling case re-scaled to $73 million, with dollar-bill serial numbers as the release code
entries.t: Vietnamese investigators now put the transnational diamond-smuggling network at $73 million of stones moved into the country, of which about $57 million have been identified, with more than 30 people arrested or detained. The stone count is unchanged from earlier reporting at more than 28,000 diamonds carried on 141 separate occasions since 2024. The figure in the charge sheet reported on 16 July was 280 billion dong, about $10.65 million, against 22 people charged. Couriers carried stones in luggage, shoes and clothing on commercial flights from Hong Kong into Vietnamese airports, with orders and prices arranged over WhatsApp, and released goods only to a recipient holding a US dollar bill whose eleven-character serial number matched one agreed in advance. Goods typically moved at about a third below market. State-owned Saigon Jewelry Company, which sets Vietnam's benchmark gold price, bought more than 3,400 of the stones for about $19 million. Police believe the operation was directed by an Indian national living in Hong Kong, sourcing in India and consolidating in Hong Kong. The former director of P-Lab, the grading subsidiary wholly owned by Phu Nhuan Jewelry that handles about 70% of Vietnamese certification, is among those charged.
entries.s: IDEX Online / South China Morning Post / Bloomberg / Nikkei Asia

entries.h: Chinese gold jewellery demand falls to its lowest second quarter since 2004
entries.t: The World Gold Council's Gold Demand Trends for the second quarter of 2026, published 30 July, put mainland Chinese gold jewellery demand at 50.0 tonnes, down 28% from 69.2 tonnes a year earlier and the lowest second-quarter figure since 2004. First-half Chinese demand was 136 tonnes, down 30%, while the value of that demand rose 11% to about $21 billion. India took 75.1 tonnes in the quarter, down 15% and its lowest second quarter since the pandemic, on first-half demand of 141 tonnes worth about $21 billion, up 26% by value. The Middle East fell 19% to 32.2 tonnes and the United States fell 25% to 22.2 tonnes, the sharpest percentage decline among the major markets. Global jewellery fabrication was 278.2 tonnes against 335.3 tonnes a year earlier, which the council described as one of the weakest second quarters in its data series. First-half global jewellery value reached about $86 billion, up 22% from $71 billion.

entries.h: Metals reopen higher after the weekend, with silver leading at $58.05
entries.t: The first session since Friday's close opened higher across the precious complex. At 6:01am New York time on 3 August, Kitco's spot page had gold bid at $4,053.30 an ounce, up $11.60 or 0.29% against the 31 July 5pm close of $4,041.70, on a range of $4,045.80 to $4,083.50. Silver bid $58.05, up 61.1 cents or 1.06%, on a range of $57.68 to $58.76, the largest percentage gain of the four metals and a gold to silver ratio of about 69.8. Platinum bid $1,647.00, up $3.00 or 0.18%, on a range of $1,641.00 to $1,676.00. Palladium bid $1,259.00, up $3.00 or 0.24%, on a wide range of $1,257.00 to $1,322.00. The week holds the ADP employment report midweek and non-farm payrolls on Friday, the first complete read on American hiring since the Federal Reserve held rates on 29 July with three dissents. This tape prints the live quotation rather than the settlement because Friday's close had already been carried through two editions.

entries.h: Michael Hill lifts revenue 2% and same-store sales 3% while closing eight stores
entries.t: Michael Hill reported group revenue of A$654.7 million, about $459.5 million, for the financial year to 28 June 2026, an increase of 2%. Same-store sales rose 3% across the group: 7% in Canada, described by the company as a record, on segment revenue of C$169.3 million; 4.8% in Australia on A$364.6 million; and 3.6% in New Zealand on NZ$108.9 million. The chain closed eight stores over the year, four in Australia and two each in Canada and New Zealand, and opened two, one in Australia and one in Canada, ending with 281 stores: 157 in Australia, 81 in Canada and 43 in New Zealand. Chief executive Jonathan Waecker said growth was significantly accelerating in Canada and New Zealand in the second half. Earnings were not disclosed alongside the sales figures.

entries.h: Shoplifting falls while fraud, organised crime and violence against jewellers rise
entries.t: The National Retail Federation's Impact of Retail Theft and Violence study, published in late July 2026, found shoplifting incidents down 12.4% in 2025 and merchandise theft down 8.1% against 2024, while 69% of retailers reported an increase in phone scams, 42% in gift-card theft and fraud, 40% in organised retail crime driving shoplifting, 36% in cargo and supply-chain theft, and 50% in repeat offenders. Jewellery, gold and watches rank among the categories generating the highest dollar losses to organised retail crime groups. The Jewelers' Security Alliance annual crime report, published 13 May 2026, counted 1,233 crimes against United States jewellery firms in 2025, down 13% from 1,420, on total dollar losses of $144.7 million against $142.5 million. On-premises burglaries fell 14% to 262 and robberies were flat at 218. Robberies involving guns, mace or vehicles rose to 27% of the total from 17%; mace or pepper-spray incidents went from 3 to 14; vehicles driven into stores went from none reported in 2024 to 13; crimes at jewellers' homes rose from 4 to 11; and two people in the industry died in 2025 against four the year before.
entries.s: JCK / National Jeweler / National Retail Federation / Jewelers' Security Alliance

entries.h: Anglo says no bidder holds exclusivity on De Beers, and rules out a listing
entries.t: Duncan Wanblad, chief executive of Anglo American, said the De Beers disposal is in the final phases of its process and that this is also the most challenging phase because several parties must move together. He put completion in the second half of 2026, with regulatory approval taking roughly a year after signature. Wanblad said Anglo is not exclusive with any consortium and retains multiple active bidders, contradicting reports that the group assembled by former De Beers chief executive Gareth Penny had been selected as front-runner. He also ruled out a public listing, saying the market lacks the capacity to absorb a De Beers flotation, confirming that the exit will be a private sale with no continuing disclosure obligation. De Beers reported first-half revenue of $1.6 billion, down 19% year on year, and an underlying EBITDA loss of $113 million, narrowed from $189 million in the first half of 2025 on cost reductions rather than recovered demand. Reports in late July put a prospective sale near $1 billion with about $750 million payable up front.

entries.h: EU natural diamonds enter the US at zero percent while lab-grown pays everywhere
entries.t: The Section 301 tariff schedule that took effect at midnight on July 24, 2026 applies duties of 10% to 12.5% to roughly 60 countries on forced-labour grounds, but exempts loose natural diamonds cut in the European Union at 0%, along with rough and polished coloured gemstones and natural pearls from the bloc. Lab-grown diamonds received no exemption from any listed country. Raw and semi-manufactured gold, silver, platinum and palladium are exempt from all 60. Karen Rentmeesters, chief executive of the Antwerp World Diamond Centre, said the exemption follows from there being no US mining or cutting industry to protect. Belgium exported $2.1 billion of polished diamonds to the United States in 2024. The Belgian flow has been repriced three times in eleven months: a 10% reciprocal duty from September 2025 until it was ruled unlawful in February, a 10% Section 122 surcharge from February to July 24, and the Section 301 schedule since. India, Canada, Mexico, Pakistan, Sri Lanka and the United Kingdom pay 10%; Angola, Australia, China, Colombia, Hong Kong, Israel, South Africa, Thailand, Turkey and the UAE pay 12.5%; Brazil carries 37.5%; Canadian polished diamonds face 50% separately from August 19.

entries.h: Central banks buy 289 tonnes in a record second quarter, but the half is the weakest since 2022
entries.t: The World Gold Council's Gold Demand Trends, published on 30 July 2026, put central bank net purchases at 289 tonnes in the second quarter, up 62% on the 177.9 tonnes bought a year earlier and a record for any second quarter. That was a fivefold increase on a first quarter revised down to 57 tonnes, leaving the first half at 345 tonnes, the smallest first half since 2022's 241 tonnes. The National Bank of Poland was the largest buyer at 51 tonnes, taking its half-year total to 82 tonnes against a self-set reserve target of about 700 tonnes. The People's Bank of China added 33 tonnes, its largest quarterly addition since the fourth quarter of 2023, lifting reported holdings to 2,346 tonnes. Uzbekistan took 16 tonnes, Kazakhstan 15, and Jordan and the Czech Republic 6 each. The Bank of Russia was the largest seller at 22 tonnes, attributed to a federal budget deficit, with Turkey selling 4 tonnes and reducing swaps from more than 80 to around 60, and the Bundesbank 1 tonne. The council's survey has 89% of reserve managers expecting official holdings to rise over the next twelve months.

entries.h: Gold demand flat at 1,269 tonnes while the half-year sets a record $380 billion by value
entries.t: Total gold demand in the second quarter of 2026 was unchanged year on year at 1,269 tonnes, and the first half reached 2,522 tonnes, up 2% on the same period of 2025. Measured by value rather than weight, the first half set a record of roughly $380 billion, the gap between the two measures being entirely the price. The composition was a substitution: central banks took 289 tonnes, up 62%, while jewellery fabrication fell to 278 tonnes, the weakest quarter since the pandemic, with Indian jewellery demand down 15% by weight to 75.1 tonnes even as the value of that demand rose about 50%. Gold closed July at $4,041.70 on the Kitco 5pm New York close, its first monthly gain since February, so the second half opens with a cost base above the average that produced the record first-half figure. No session has traded since; the tape carries unchanged into a week holding the ADP employment report midweek and non-farm payrolls on Friday.
entries.s: World Gold Council / Kitco / City Index / FX Leaders

entries.h: TAGS tenders clear between 75% and 100% depending on stone size
entries.t: TAGS reported four summer tender outcomes that describe two different rough markets. A Zimbabwean parcel offered in Dubai in early June cleared 100%, with prices firm in higher qualities and slightly lower in the bottom ranges. An Angolan sale of stones 10.8 carats and above, drawing material from ten deposits plus the full run-of-mine output of one further seller, cleared 95% and realised $21.7 million. South African run-of-mine goods sold through June and July in Johannesburg cleared about 75% per tender despite record participant attendance. The most recent Dubai sale, of large South African production, cleared better than 80% and realised $15.2 million on extremely high attendance. The house said prices again exceeded the participating mines' expectations. The pattern places large sorted stones sold internationally at or near full clearance and smaller variable parcels, the segment most exposed to lab-grown competition, a quarter unsold.

entries.h: NY Now opens under Rockview ownership as Bain names jewellery luxury's strongest category
entries.t: NY Now's summer market opened at the Javits Center on August 2 and runs to August 4, the first edition since Rockview Management Group acquired the show from Emerald, with chief executive Dorothy Belshaw leading. More than 70 exhibitors are new or returning after a hiatus, and over 90 brands and makers from 19 countries are exhibiting. Fine jewellery sits in the Luxury Lifestyle section, carrying Brooke Gregson, Heather B. Moore, Bondeye Jewelry, Eden Presley, Carolina Neves, Dana Kellin and Annette Ferdinandsen, and in Curated for emerging designers; exhibitors include Dilamani, Hine Fine Jewelry, J Fields Jewelry, Jacob Keleher Jewelry, Lauren Newton Jewelry, Tacit Fine Jewelry, Jewels by Sanjam, Jessica Liu Designs and Yael Sonia. Attendance figures were not published. Separately, the spring Bain and Altagamma Luxury Goods Worldwide Market Study put personal luxury goods at €358 billion in 2025, down from €364 billion, and forecast €365 billion to €373 billion in 2026, growth of 2% to 4%, within a total luxury market of €1.44 trillion to €1.47 trillion growing between nothing and 2% at constant rates. Jewellery was named the strongest category, with US luxury brands up 10% to 15% year on year in the first quarter, Europe the weak link on tourism, China recovering slowly and Japan slowing.
entries.s: National Jeweler / InStore / Gifts & Decorative Accessories / Bain & Company / GJEPC Solitaire / WWD

entries.h: Russia bans the word diamond for synthetic stones from September 1
entries.t: Russian Government Resolution No. 657, signed on May 30 and taking effect on September 1, 2026, prohibits the word diamond and all its derivatives in consumer-facing descriptions of synthetic stones sold in Russia. Tags must carry the word synthetic or the abbreviation Synth., and the approved term is cut synthetic diamond. The words precious, real, genuine, natural, mined, mineral and eco-friendly are struck from all consumer information, along with colour and clarity descriptors borrowed from natural grading. Weight must be given in grams; carat weight is prohibited for synthetics, making a one-carat stone a 0.2 gram stone. Tags must also carry product name, maker or importer, country of origin, model number, total weight, metal and fineness, stone particulars and a unique identification number matching a two-dimensional barcode. Deputy finance minister Alexey Moiseev said the aim is to improve transparency and protect consumers. CIBJO is expected to mandate the same single term at its September 4 congress.
entries.s: Alrosa / Rapaport / Solitaire GJEPC / The Retail Jeweller India

entries.h: Gold closes July at $4,041.70, its first monthly gain since February
entries.t: Kitco's 5pm New York close on July 31 put spot gold at $4,041.70 an ounce, down $60.90 or 1.48% on the session, the weakest day of the week, as the dollar rebounded from a six-week low and traders unwound the rally that followed the Federal Reserve's hold. Across July the metal still finished about 0.5% higher, its first monthly gain since February and the end of a four-month losing run. Trading Economics puts gold 20.22% above a year earlier. The white metals fell harder: silver $57.44, down 2.45%, platinum $1,644.00, down 0.60%, and palladium $1,256.00, down 3.38%, putting the gold-silver ratio near 70.4 and platinum at roughly 41% of the gold price. From this edition the tape carries the Kitco 5pm close as its single reference point, replacing mixed intraday prints.
entries.s: Kitco / Kitco News / CNBC / Trading Economics

entries.h: DMCC sets the second Dubai Diamond Week for October 26 to 29
entries.t: DMCC will hold the second edition of Dubai Diamond Week from October 26 to 29, 2026, four days of conference sessions alongside a sourcing exhibition co-hosted with the Italian Exhibition Group, with governments, producers, manufacturers, retailers, traders, investors and technology firms invited. Dubai's diamond trade reached a record $41.7 billion and 359.5 million carats in 2025, with natural stones accounting for 95.8% of traded value, and the Dubai Diamond Exchange now anchors an ecosystem of close to 1,400 companies and the largest tender facility in the business. The event follows a year in which the 41st World Diamond Congress met in Dubai, Okavango Diamond Company signed a tender arrangement with the exchange, and Qatar's new bourse joined the World Federation of Diamond Bourses.
entries.s: DMCC / Solitaire GJEPC / Arabian Business / InStore

entries.h: Hermès holds watches flat at €269 million while jewellery and home grow 5.4%
entries.t: Hermès reported first-half 2026 watch revenue of €269 million, down 4.2% as published but up 0.2% at constant exchange rates, with second-quarter watch sales of €134 million up 3.0% published and 4.4% at constant rates. Other Hermès sectors, the segment carrying jewellery and home, took €1.065 billion in the half, up 0.8% published and 5.4% at constant rates, with the second quarter up 4.0%. Group revenue was €8.2 billion, up 6.1% at constant rates, with recurring operating income of €3.4 billion, an operating margin of 41.0% and net profit of €2.2 billion. The Americas grew 15.3% at constant rates and Japan 11.0%, while the Middle East fell 4.2%. Separately, Bucherer confirmed it will operate Rolex's Fifth Avenue flagship in Manhattan, reported by WatchPro at 43,000 square feet over four floors.
entries.s: Hermès / Retail Insight Network / WatchPro / JCK

entries.h: De Beers India runs Friendship Day across 60 stores as tonnage falls 15%
entries.t: De Beers India launched the second edition of its Love, from Bestie campaign for Friendship Day, running August 1 and 2 across 60 retail partner stores including Forevermark outlets in Mumbai, Delhi, Bengaluru, Chennai, Pune, Kanpur, Kochi, Coimbatore and Nagpur. The collection is four natural diamond bracelet designs made to be worn in pairs, including a signature piece spelling BFF in Morse code with baguette and round stones, supported by a three-station in-store experience. The backdrop is Indian jewellery demand down 15% by weight in the second quarter, to 75.1 tonnes from 88.8 tonnes, with the value of that demand up about 50% on record gold prices. Separately, supplier Sy Kessler launched a watch battery starter kit from $235 on the arithmetic that a cell costs about $1 and the job sells for more than $15.
entries.s: The Retail Jeweller India / Medianews4u / Business Standard / JCK

entries.h: De Beers narrows its half-year loss to $188 million as the rough index holds flat
entries.t: Anglo American's interim results put De Beers revenue at $1.58 billion for the first half of 2026, down 19% year on year, with an underlying loss of $188 million, 23% narrower than a year earlier, and an underlying EBITDA loss of $113 million, 40% smaller. Sales volumes fell 20%. The consolidated average realised price fell 32% to $105 a carat on a lower-value sales mix and a rough price index 16% below last year, but the index barely moved within the half at 68 in the first quarter and 69 in the second. Unit costs fell 26% to $64 a carat, capital expenditure fell 33% to $115 million, and annual overheads are more than $100 million lighter than in 2024. The trading division swung to $30 million of underlying EBITDA from a $260 million loss. Anglo's chief executive said the sale process is in its final and most challenging phase and declined to name a buyer.
entries.s: Rapaport / National Jeweler / JCK / Anglo American

entries.h: Gold ends July at $4,054.68, giving back the post-Fed rally on a dollar bounce
entries.t: Spot gold fell about 1.19% to $4,054.68 an ounce on July 31 after prints earlier in the session held above $4,086, as the dollar rebounded from a six-week trough and traders booked the previous day's gains. Thursday had seen the metal crest $4,100 following the Federal Reserve's hold. Gold finished the month roughly 1.4% higher and is 20.57% up year on year. Silver fell 1.72% to $57.99, platinum 1.46% to $1,636 and palladium 1.53% to $1,288.50, putting the gold-silver ratio near 69.9. Fine gold at that level costs about $130 a gram before making charges.

entries.h: Second-quarter jewellery demand falls to 278 tonnes, the lightest since the pandemic
entries.t: World Gold Council figures published on July 30 put global gold jewellery demand at 278 tonnes in the second quarter, down 17% year on year and the lowest quarterly volume since the pandemic, while the value of that demand rose 14% to $40 billion. Total demand was flat at 1,269 tonnes: bar and coin steady at 307 tonnes, central banks buying 289 tonnes in a sharp recovery from the first quarter, and exchange-traded funds shedding 45 tonnes. The quarter's average London price was $4,506.29 an ounce, roughly 10% above where gold traded at the end of July, and the first half set a record for the value of gold demand at $380 billion.

entries.h: India's jewellery demand falls 15% to 75.1 tonnes as the value of the bill rises 50%
entries.t: Indian gold jewellery demand fell to 75.1 tonnes in the second quarter from 88.8 tonnes a year earlier, a 15% decline by weight, while total Indian gold demand fell 6% and the value of that demand rose about 50% on record prices. Investment demand held up as jewellery gave way, the same split visible in the global figures. The context is a counter running on recycled metal and price-led revenue: Indian gold fell about 10% in June to a six-month low near 141,000 rupees per 10 grams, listed jewellers reported 30% to 60% revenue growth, old-gold trade-ins now fund up to 55% of counter sales, and June gem and jewellery exports rose 26.5% to $2.21 billion with gold jewellery up 54.5%.
entries.s: World Gold Council / IBTimes India / KNN India

entries.h: Gemfields lifts first-half auction revenue 72% to $102.9 million on emerald
entries.t: Gemfields reported auction revenue of $102.9 million for the first half of 2026, up 72% year on year. Kagem in Zambia held premium emerald output, and its higher-quality rough auction in May took $26.8 million, selling 36 of 37 lots and 183,385 of 185,135 carats offered at an average $146.08 a carat. A mixed-quality ruby sale in February added $53 million from 121 of 135 lots. At Montepuez in Mozambique, premium-grade ruby recovery ran at 0.025 carats per tonne; the company is redirecting mining to higher-potential areas and has commissioned a new processing plant expected to reach full capacity later in 2026. Net debt stood at $44.2 million on June 30, before $33.3 million of auction receivables. Full results are due on September 25.
entries.s: Rapaport / TipRanks / National Jeweler / Gemfields Group

entries.h: Anglo's price for De Beers comes in at about $1 billion
entries.t: Bloomberg reported on July 29 that the Global Diamond Consortium, led by former De Beers chief executive Gareth Penny and including the governments of Namibia and Angola, would pay about $1 billion for Anglo American's 85% stake: roughly $750 million on closing and $250 million deferred, plus some $500 million of working capital injected into the business. De Beers carried a book value of about $2.3 billion earlier this year after $3.5 billion of write-downs, against a $17.6 billion valuation at the 2001 take-private. Botswana holds the remaining 15%. Terms are not final; Anglo still expects to close by the end of 2026.

entries.h: Gold recovers to $4,074.98 the day after the Fed's hawkish hold
entries.t: Spot gold rose about 0.22% to $4,074.98 an ounce on July 30, roughly $46 above Wednesday's post-FOMC level of $4,029 and back inside its pre-meeting range; the metal is 23.84% higher year on year. Silver eased 0.25% to $57.79 from $57.94 and the gold-silver ratio widened to 70.37 from 70.22. Central-bank buying of 244 tonnes in the first quarter and 41 tonnes in May continues to underpin the dips.

entries.h: Platinum jumps 1.62% to $1,628.20 as Kevin Reilly retires from PGI USA
entries.t: Platinum rose 1.62% to $1,628.20 an ounce, up 1.77% on the month and 26.13% year on year, with palladium 2.51% higher at $1,284.00 — a reversal of Wednesday's cooling in the white metals. Analysts still forecast a fourth consecutive annual supply deficit; January's all-time high was $2,923.70. Against that, global platinum jewellery demand is expected to contract about 6% in 2026, led by China, with India facing tariff headwinds. Platinum Guild International USA announced on July 28 that senior vice president Kevin Reilly had retired at the end of June after twenty years there and a thirty-nine-year career, having established platinum programmes at GIA, Pratt, SCAD, RISD, the 92Y Jewelry Center and the Miami Jewelry School.

entries.h: Heritage books a record $1.41 billion half and its largest jewelry sale ever
entries.t: Heritage Auctions took more than $1.41 billion in the first six months of 2026, up 47% year on year and the highest midyear total in its fifty-year history. Its Spring Fine Jewelry Signature auction on May 4 realised $9,713,640, the highest-grossing jewelry auction in the firm's history, beating the $9.2 million set in September 2025. The top lot was a platinum ring set with a 6.59-carat octagonal Kashmir sapphire at $906,250, more than $300,000 above its high estimate. Across the majors, first-half global sales at Christie's, Sotheby's and Phillips rose 70% to $6.8 billion with fees, with Sotheby's alone at a record $4.4 billion.
entries.s: ARTnews / Intelligent Collector / National Jeweler / The Art Newspaper

entries.h: All four Swiss groups turn positive year on year for the first time since early 2022
entries.t: Morgan Stanley's second-quarter index of Swiss watch secondary-market prices rose 1.5%, and all four groups it tracks are now positive year on year for the first time since early 2022: Swatch Group up 5.4% and Richemont up 4.2%. Sequentially in the quarter, Richemont gained 1.3% and Swatch 1.0%. April had been the market's best single month since March 2022 at plus 2.5% on the WatchCharts overall index, ahead of Watches and Wonders, before dealer supply reached record levels and demand lagged through May and June.

entries.h: Fed holds at 3.50–3.75% in a 9–3 vote; gold eases to $4,029
entries.t: The FOMC held rates on July 29 with three presidents — Hammack, Kashkari and Logan — dissenting for a quarter-point hike, and Chair Kevin Warsh's statement again omitted forward guidance. Gold slipped from about $4,046 to near $4,029, cushioned by central-bank buying of 244 tonnes in Q1 and 41 tonnes in May. Silver eased to ~$57.90, platinum to ~$1,597 and palladium to ~$1,248.
entries.s: CNBC / Federal Reserve / FX Leaders / Fortune

entries.h: LVMH Watches & Jewellery is the group's best division at €5.23B, +9% organic
entries.t: LVMH's Watches & Jewellery arm posted €5.23 billion in first-half sales, up about 9% organically with an 11% second quarter and recurring operating profit up 9% to €831 million, led by Tiffany and Bulgari across the US, Asia and Japan. Overall group revenue fell 3% to €38.6 billion, making jewelry the standout as fashion, leather, beauty and spirits softened.

entries.h: Kering's jewelry houses grow 14% to €521M as the group slips 3%
entries.t: Kering's jewelry division (Boucheron, Pomellato, Qeelin, DoDo) lifted first-half revenue 14% to €521 million, up 20% on a comparable basis, with operating income doubling to €32 million and directly operated retail up 28% comparable. Boucheron reached record levels on Japan and the Quatre XS launch. Group revenue fell 3% to €7.22 billion.

entries.h: Petra's Q4 revenue caves 44% to $38M; Finsch enters business rescue
entries.t: Petra Diamonds reported fourth-quarter FY2026 revenue of $38 million, down 44% from $68 million, on weak tender prices and a small-goods mix. Consolidated net debt rose to $322 million from $298 million; a R300 million facility runs to early 2028 and $6 million of July interest was deferred to January 2027. The Finsch mine was suspended and placed in business rescue in June.

entries.h: Gem Diamonds' big stones lift the Q1 2026 average price ~17% to ~$1,501/ct
entries.t: Gem Diamonds' Letšeng mine kept producing high-value stones as the broader market stayed soft, lifting the average price in the first quarter of 2026 about 17% to roughly $1,501 a carat from $1,288 the quarter before. Recoveries included a 191.82-carat Type IIa white and a 100.71-carat faint yellow; a parcel of ten stones over 10.8 carats brought $7 million and one 52.24-carat white sold at $32,908 a carat, the mirror image of Petra's quarter. Corrected 24 August 2026: this entry and the article carried the $1,501 average with no period label. It is a first-quarter figure and was correct for that quarter. Gem Diamonds' first-half average, published 28 July 2026, is $1,395 a carat on 42,624 carats sold, up 38% from $1,008.
entries.s: Rapaport / MINING.COM / Gem Diamonds H1 2026 trading update, 28 July 2026

entries.h: Gold idles near $4,046 on the eve of the Fed decision
entries.t: Spot gold traded in a tight $4,021–$4,080 range into the July 28–29 FOMC, with CME FedWatch pricing a 62% chance of a hold at 3.50–3.75% and 38% of a quarter-point hike, and roughly 81% odds of a September move. Second-quarter GDP, personal income and spending, and core PCE near 3.3% follow on Thursday. Palladium jumped ~3.3% and platinum ~1.7% on Monday; silver held near $58.50 with $60 in view.

entries.h: Titan's June quarter revenue rises about 41% — a third straight 40%-plus
entries.t: Titan Company reported roughly 41% revenue growth for the quarter to June 2026, its third consecutive quarter above 40%. The jewellery division (Tanishq, Mia, CaratLane) grew about 39% with plain and studded each up in the mid-thirties and strong coin demand; watches rose 23% (analogue high-twenties, smart watches down low-teens), eyewear 23%, emerging businesses 19% and the international business 128%. Buyer growth was in the early double digits while average ticket sizes rose in the high double digits amid stable gold prices.

entries.h: Collective Horology takes the US tariffs to the Court of International Trade
entries.t: The California watch retailer, joined by spice importer Burlap & Barrel and backed by the Liberty Justice Center, sued to challenge the Section 301 duties, arguing the US Trade Representative applied a near-uniform tariff across dozens of countries without the country-by-country analysis the 1974 Trade Act requires. Swiss watch imports have run at least 12.5% more expensive since April 2025; Collective says it is owed more than $164,000 in refunds from the vacated IEEPA tariffs, on top of Section 122 and 301 duties paid.

entries.h: Qatar launches its first diamond exchange at Ras Bufontas
entries.t: The Qatar Free Zones Authority launched the Qatar Diamond Exchange, a Kimberley Process-compliant hub near Doha offering trading licences, on-site sorting and independent valuation, secure vaulting, specialist insurance and participation in rough and polished tenders. Qatar became a full KP member in 2021 and in 2025 named the free-zone authority the sole authorized entry and exit point for rough. CEO Sheikh Mohammed Bin Hamad Bin Faisal Al-Thani framed it as bringing the full value chain into one regulated ecosystem — a Gulf rival to Dubai's record $41.7 billion 2025 trade.

entries.h: GemGuide lifts Mozambique ruby prices and regrades Burma stones
entries.t: The colored-stone pricing service raised Mozambique ruby prices sharply on strong demand for unenhanced, untreated material sold by tender, and abandoned its traditional one-to-ten scale for unenhanced Burmese ruby, pricing only four grades — Middle Commercial, Lower Good, Upper Fine and Upper Extra Fine. Research director Stuart Robertson said fine Mogok material is now so scarce that availability matters more than price. The revisions are live in the app and appear in the July–August issue.

entries.h: Israel Diamond Exchange president resigns as exports hit a record low
entries.t: Nissim Zuaretz stepped down after two years as first-half 2026 diamond exports fell to $2.4 billion, the lowest on record and a fraction of the roughly $7 billion shipped at the 2015 peak. He cited dealers and goods relocating to Dubai, lab-grown competition, weak demand and a new US tariff effective July 24. Corrected 25 August 2026: that duty is the Section 301 forced-labour tariff and Israel's rate under it is 12.5%, not the 10% originally printed, which was the Section 122 surcharge sunsetting the same day, warning that without change the exchange could disappear. A successor election is expected in November.

entries.h: CIBJO expects to replace 'lab-grown' with 'synthetic'
entries.t: The world jewelry confederation expects to strike 'laboratory-grown' and 'laboratory-created' from its Blue Book and require 'synthetic' for man-made stones, with a formal decision at its September 4 congress. Charles Abouchar of the colored-stone commission framed the goal as protecting consumer confidence through clearer language. The move follows Russia (from September 1), the African producers (May), India's BIS and the GIA's 2025 update.

entries.h: Small-diamond recovery accelerates — 0.30ct index up 4.2% in June
entries.t: The RapNet Diamond Index for 0.30-carat stones rose 4.2% in June, up from 2.1% in May, and half-carat goods added 1.3%, while the one-carat slipped 0.7% and three-carat edged up 0.4%. Inventory reductions, steady US retail demand and firm Hong Kong counters drove the correction; De Beers cut rough under 0.75 carats, and 2025 global rough production fell 8% to 98.8 million carats.

entries.h: Morgan Stanley: only Patek, Rolex and AP hold value above retail
entries.t: The bank's Q2 read (WatchCharts, June 29) put value retention at 15.4% above retail for Patek Philippe, 9.8% for Rolex and 3.0% for Audemars Piguet, with every other tracked brand below list — Cartier −27.4%, Omega −32.3%, IWC −37.9%. Patek's Aquanaut trades ~90% over retail and the Nautilus 74%; Rolex's Oyster Perpetual 35% over. Gains remain modest outside the big three.

entries.h: China imports about 173 tonnes of gold in June
entries.t: China's June bullion imports reached roughly 173 tonnes, the strongest monthly inflow since March 2024, lifting first-half imports toward 820 tonnes as softer prices revived demand. The buying helped gold defend the low $4,000s into the Federal Reserve's July 28–29 meeting, which sits alongside second-quarter GDP and core PCE inflation seen near 3.3%.

entries.h: US jewelry sales rise 8.6% in H1 as the average ticket climbs ~19%
entries.t: US retail jewelry revenue rose 8.6% over the first half of 2026 and 13% year on year in June, with the average purchase price up about 19% for the half and 20% in June (Tenoris).
